epics.title: Send the week-one license paperwork and inventory content rights
epics.summary: The two third-party licenses with long tails (Ableton Link proprietary grant, Steinberg ASIO agreement) are requested in week one, and the demo content's missing content license is inventoried so the Commons seeding decision (R11, R4) is not discovered in Phase 4.
epics.exit: Link, rusty_link relicense and ASIO requests sent in week one and logged in LOG.md, each with a follow-up issue that owns the reply; a rights inventory of the four demos classifies every instrument as original, licensed-library or provenance-to-confirm, keeps the naming patterns and author statements in the private record, and states the open question for the company in a counsel-cleared public projection.

epics.title: Turn the open questions into dated decision records
epics.summary: Phase 0 exists to turn Q1 to Q14 into decisions with dates (09-roadmap principle 4). This epic creates the decision-record convention and records every decision that needs no experiment: the company questions, the closed questions, platform floors, the 1.9.6 reference-behavior ruling that determinism and the port fixes depend on, and the go/no-go gate.
epics.exit: design/v2-proposal/decisions/ holds a dated record for every Q1 to Q14 row and for the go/no-go gate, each with alternatives and evidence.

epics.title: Prove a Rust binary can link the engine statically and play the test project on three OS
epics.summary: The spike that seeds xj-engine-sys: a minimal C target with an install rule, a 300-line Rust program that links it from build.rs and plays the test project through cpal, and a CI matrix on Windows, macOS and Linux. Retires the toolchain unknowns (libclang, MSVC CRT, PIC, static linking) before Phase 1 commits to the ABI shape.
epics.exit: The Rust spike program plays the engine test project on all three platforms in CI; a report names the toolchain facts the xj-engine-sys spec inherits.

epics.title: Check in the craft-timing harness and repeat the measurement on a 2019 laptop
epics.summary: The second pass measured craft at 28 ms worst case on a fast machine; the remaining risk (R3's retired contingency) is a slow laptop and the largest content. Check the harness into the engine tree so anyone can reproduce the numbers from the tree (and the Phase 1 CI bench job reproduces them in Release), extend it to dump per-segment delta and intensity (which also proves the delta regression at runtime), and measure on a 2019 laptop.
epics.exit: The harness builds as an engine target and its numbers are reproducible from the tree (smoke-run in CI today, reproduced in Release by the Phase 1 CI bench job), and the 2019-laptop measurement is recorded with a decision on the commit-horizon contingency.

epics.title: Build the same performance-surface slice in Tauri 2 and iced on three OS and score it
epics.summary: The decision with the highest product impact and least certainty (R2, Q1). Both candidates render the same slice (scenes grid, harmony strip with a live commit-horizon line, ten layer strips with 60 fps meters (05 §Buses allocates all ten; 05's slice sentence said four), 200 timeline elements) from one fake snapshot stream, on Windows, macOS and Linux, and are scored against the eight criteria in 05-workstation.
epics.exit: Both slices run on all three platforms; a scored criteria table and the Q1 decision record exist; the surface's view-model contract is written down so re-hosting is a UI rewrite, not a product rewrite.

epics.title: Run the blind stretch and pitch-shift bake-off on fixed material
epics.summary: Retires R6 before any DSP code depends on a library: Signalsmith Stretch (MIT, vendored from upstream since the crate pins a 2025-06 commit) against Bungee (MPL-2.0, driven through a small C++ driver over its granular API because the Rust binding was archived in 2026-03), on the fixed material of 11-resolutions Q2, judged blind by three musicians.
epics.exit: Rendered comparison sets exist for both libraries; the blind listening result and the Q2 decision are recorded.

epics.title: Lock a Rust process to an MPC and Ableton Live and measure beat-to-DAC alignment
epics.summary: Retires the clock unknowns before xj-transport exists: a real-hardware lock demo of rusty_link 0.4.9 (vendored Link 4.0.0b3) against an MPC One and Ableton Live with a packet capture of the MPC interoperation, the AUDIOENGINE-1 loopback measurement per audio host against Link's 3 ms tolerance, and the dated Q3 record: the epoch design that follows from Link sharing phase and tempo but not beat magnitude, the Link 4.1.1 pin and the plan for a Phase 2 binding fork (whose 4.1.1 interoperability capture belongs to p2-xport-link-binding-fork).
epics.exit: An MPC and Live lock to the Rust process on a LAN; per-host DAC alignment is measured; the epoch and Link-path decision record exists.

epics.title: Draft xj-base@1 from the demo conventions and have the first pack authors review it
epics.summary: Q4 resolved to codifying technical conventions, not moods; the people who will author the first packs review the list before it is versioned in Phase 4. Keeps the Commons small and agreed (R4).
epics.exit: A reviewed xj-base@1 draft with the amendments of the first pack authors and the Q4 decision record.

epics.title: Verify what midir exposes and how the two reference 4x4 controllers light up
epics.summary: The mapping design in 08-performer-input keys profiles on manufacturer and product, which midir 0.11 cannot provide, and the LED protocols of the Launchpad Mini MK3 and MPD218 are only partly documented. Verify on hardware before xj-control is designed.
epics.exit: A per-OS table of midir identity strings for both controllers, a working Device Inquiry handshake, and hardware-verified LED behavior for both devices.

epics.title: Set up the V2 tracker and a Rust CI baseline on three OS
epics.summary: Nothing in the repository today carries a `v2`, phase or area label, the 1.10 milestone is a 41-issue parking lot, and no Rust CI exists. Create the tracker structure the roadmap requires and a three-OS Rust CI baseline so every later spike and crate lands under test from day one (R13).
epics.exit: Labels, milestones and the project exist with issue-dependency support; a Rust workspace skeleton passes fmt, clippy and nextest on Windows, macOS and Linux.

epics.title: Make craft deterministic: tests first, engine-owned randomness, one swap PR
epics.summary: R9 in task order: stable store iteration, determinism tests written red before any generator changes, engine-owned RNG primitives (because std distributions and std::shuffle are implementation-defined and differ across libc++, libstdc++ and MSVC), then one PR that threads the generator through all seven construction sites with no other change. Per-engine ids and sub-seeds follow, and the segment-store JSON dump used by every golden comparison lives here.
epics.exit: Same seed, project and overrides produce byte-identical sorted store dumps per platform, and identical dumps across the three CI platforms after excluding or rounding the documented floating-point fields (intensity, micros); the craft matrix passed on every commit of the swap.

epics.title: Fix the C++ port regressions that the 2.0 features would otherwise be built on
epics.summary: The gap map found behaviors where the C++ 1.9.6 port diverged from the Java original: a persistence window of 3.6 ms, a delta that never advances (intensity pinned at 0.2, main programs never rotating), store puts that never overwrite, a mute roll that throws at probability 1, broken delta arcs, a UB sort comparator, 32-bit micros on MSVC. Cues, follow mode and the determinism goldens depend on these being fixed under the recorded reference-behavior ruling; the mute bound, Transition label and intensityLayers check are Java parity and crash-class removals. The richer Beat/Detail fixture is built here too, since the determinism goldens and the follow test both consume it. The Unreal plugin's C++ compile guard lands here, before the micros widening and lifecycle changes alter the surfaces it uses (Q8).
epics.exit: Each fix has a regression test; the craft matrix and the updated foundation fixtures pass; 1.9.x demo content loads with correct voice and track names.

epics.title: Ship the C ABI core: header, lifecycle, cycle, status, build target, C-compiler test
epics.summary: The contract every Rust crate and third-party host builds on: `engine/include/xjmusic/xj_c.h` with the register's conventions, lifecycle that actually clears the store and loads from memory, the flat schedule-event struct, failure propagation and a log callback, the `xjmusic_c` CMake target with install rules, and a C test program compiled with a C compiler on three platforms.
epics.exit: A C11 program compiled with cc, clang and cl links the installed `xjmusic_c` archive, loads a project from memory, runs cycles and receives events on all three CI platforms.

epics.title: Run the ABI under sanitizers and fuzz it, and freeze ABI 1.0.0 behind a semver check
epics.summary: R8 mitigation in order: the gtest and C tests run under AddressSanitizer and UBSan on every PR, then libFuzzer targets cover the JSON loaders, cue sequences and foundation records, then a nightly fuzz job keeps the corpus. This decomposition starts xj-engine-sys from the C-compiler test, earlier than 09's P1->P2 order for engine-facing crates (09 parallelizes only the non-engine parts of Phase 2), so the sanitizers and fuzzers harden the ABI while it is being consumed rather than before; the baseline-and-diff check freezes ABI 1.0.0 at the tag.
epics.exit: ASan/UBSan jobs are green on PRs; fuzz targets run nightly with a persisted corpus and zero open crashers at the 2.0.0 tag; the ABI baseline diff runs on every PR after the tag.

epics.title: Implement cues with landing boundaries, the commit horizon and tempo as an input
epics.summary: Generalizes override-and-rewrite into a cue queue with boundaries (NOW, BEAT, BAR, SEGMENT, MAIN, MACRO), a commit horizon in chain micros derived from the new `commitHorizonBeats`, exact `earliest_landing` arithmetic, and the seven cue types including the new NextMain path for Advance, chord forcing with a chord-level transposition primitive that the engine lacks today, intensity ramps and a deterministic layer-mute flag. Existing overrides become wrappers so no consumer changes. Tempo joins the same epic: the External policy records the host's tempo on each new segment, the three sites that read the main program's tempo read the segment's instead, and already-crafted segments are never re-timed.
epics.exit: Every cue type lands exactly at its requested boundary and never inside the commit horizon in tests at 30, 120 and 180 bpm; EngineTest and the craft matrix still pass through the wrappers. With policy External a tempo change takes effect exactly at the next segment boundary and the 20 to 999 bpm policy is tested.

epics.title: Implement follow mode and conduct mode around the foundation seam
epics.summary: The venue-enabling engine change: a foundation record format (with the new per-segment `barBeats`, duration and a stable main-sequence identity) over the richer fixture from e1-port-fixes, conduct-mode publication, an `ExternalFoundationCraft` that writes the same store entities MacroMainCraft writes, the Fabricator answering the three direct main-program reads from the record, the Q14 barBeats candidate filter, hold-and-rejoin when the timeline runs dry, and the two-engines-one-process test that is the Phase 1 exit.
epics.exit: Two engines in one process, one conducting and one following over a fixture with beat and detail programs, produce identical key, tempo, chords, voicings and memes per segment span on three platforms; hold, fallback and rejoin are tested.

epics.title: Add preview, choice diagnostics and reachable messages
epics.summary: The legibility features: a scratch-store preview that returns what a cue would do, MarbleBag recording behind a flag with both exclusion gates covered, a monotonic message sequence so hosts can poll `since`, and per-stage craft timing as messages.
epics.exit: Preview of a cue equals the result of sending it; the why-panel data exists as namespaced SegmentMeta; messages carry sequence numbers and craft timing per stage.

epics.title: Complete the C ABI surface: snapshots, introspection, cues, tempo, foundation, preview
epics.summary: The remaining functions of the register through the ABI, each with a C test: segment and message JSON snapshots, introspection JSON, the new cue, tempo, foundation, determinism and preview groups, and the host-settable choice-diagnostics flag.
epics.exit: Every function in the contract register's list exists in xj_c.h with a C test: the register's surface is complete and C-tested (the 1.0.0 freeze itself is the baseline captured at the engine-v2.0.0 tag).

epics.title: Add the additive content fields and the craft paths that use them
epics.summary: InstrumentConfig gains allowPitchShift, pitchShiftRange and allowStretch; NotePicker gains a nearest-sample fallback that requests a shift; loop craft computes a stretch ratio; new optional entity fields are tolerated. A compatibility fixture proves every 1.9.x project loads unchanged.
epics.exit: Shifted and stretched requests appear in schedule events only when content allows them; all four demo payloads and the test project load with identical behavior when the fields are absent.

epics.title: Modernize engine CI, decouple tags, ship engine 2.0.0 and keep the Unreal plugin building
epics.summary: The release gate today requires the engine and Java workstation versions to be identical and ships a Debug Windows library with no headers. Fix the workflows, define per-component tags, ship a proper artifact layout with checksums, put the Java workstation into maintenance mode, and tag engine 2.0.0 when every exit condition is green. The Unreal plugin stays on the C++ API (Q8): the compile guard from e1-port-fixes is green before the tag, and the plugin is bumped to engine-v2.0.0 and released after it; the example player keeps building in one job as the engine's smoke test (03), and the plugin's pre-existing macOS/Linux Build.cs defect is repaired separately so the exit clause stays literal.
epics.exit: engine-v2.0.0 is tagged with header, archive, ABI manifest and checksums on four runners; the Java workstation is in maintenance mode on its own tag line. The Unreal plugin builds against engine-v2.0.0 unchanged apart from its tag.

epics.title: Update Doxygen and the docs site for engine 2.0 and the C ABI
epics.summary: Doxygen runs with a missing LICENSE.md and calls the engine a shared library; the docs site has no integration section at all. Document the C ABI and host contract, the cue and foundation model, and the Build contract where integrators look.
epics.exit: engine-docs.xjmusic.com builds clean with the C ABI documented; docs.xjmusic.com has an Integrate section covering the C++ API, the C ABI, cues, the foundation record and the Build contract.

epics.title: Lay out the Rust workspace with a dependency and license policy
epics.summary: The crate layout from 03-architecture with the MSRV, feature flags (`link`, `asio`) and a cargo-deny policy that encodes what the research found: MPL file-level obligations (symphonia, triple_buffer), GPL only behind the licensed `link` feature, banned stale codec crates, and pinned majors for the crates that churn (rubato 5 with audioadapter 5, rtrb >= 0.4).
epics.exit: The workspace builds and tests on three OS with caching; cargo-deny fails on any license or ban violation; third-party notices are generated.

epics.title: Build xj-engine-sys and the safe xj-engine wrapper
epics.summary: The generated bindings over xj_c.h with build.rs driving CMake, and the safe wrapper whose types make misuse a compile error: a `!Sync` Engine, typed events, cues and overrides as methods, typed snapshots. Becomes the only caller of the ABI (R8).
epics.exit: The Rust port of the two-engine follow test passes through the wrapper on three OS; the wrapper's unsafe surface is audited and runs under ASan.

epics.title: Read and write V1 projects as the Java workstation does, with a Java round-trip in CI
epics.summary: xj-content replaces ProjectManager: a reader over the five file kinds and the legacy single-file layout, a writer that reproduces Jackson's ordering and float formatting, V2 fields in a sidecar per the transition decision, a merged in-memory payload for the engine (which reads only `.xj` plus `build/**`), Build for engine, and the Rust port of the chord and note grammar. The Java round-trip test runs on every PR until the Java workstation is archived (R14).
epics.exit: A Java-written demo project round-trips through xj-content and back through the Java reader with semantic equality in CI; Build for engine output is format-compatible with the Java Build for the Unreal plugin (identical file names, an equivalent fmt chunk of 48 kHz/16-bit/stereo PCM (the Java Build's ffmpeg muxer adds a LIST/INFO chunk, so header bytes are not compared), semantically equal build/<slug>.json, audio compared by tolerance).

epics.title: Decode, resample and cache audio by content hash, rendering variants ahead of time
epics.summary: Replaces the Java AudioCache and ffmpeg: symphonia decoding with the features the demos need and robustness against their real chunk layouts, rubato resampling (88.2 to 48 kHz is the dominant case), a BLAKE3-keyed disk cache with eviction sized against 27.7 GB of decoded demos, variant rendering with Signalsmith on the I/O thread, and a preload worker pool.
epics.exit: All 3,000 demo WAVs decode and the 1,024 off-rate ones resample to 48 kHz with no audio-thread involvement; the cache is keyed by (contentHash, rate, channels, ratio, semitones), never resamples, renders or decodes a compressed sample twice on a machine (device-rate PCM is re-read), and gives bit-identical buffers cold or warm.

epics.title: Own the clock: four time bases, BeatClock trait, Link feature flag, event conversion
epics.summary: The one component allowed to convert between chain micros, device frames, beat time and wall time. Builds the per-stream affine maps the Phase 0 measurement showed are necessary (cpal instants do not share Link's clock on Linux), the BeatClock trait with an internal implementation, the `link` implementation under the one-writer rule, and the schedule-event-to-DSP-command conversion with a late-command counter.
epics.exit: Scheduled events become sample-accurate DSP commands; under simulated drift and tempo change the late-command counter stays at zero and beat positions match Link's phase.

epics.title: Build the real-time graph: voices, buses, master dynamics, limiter, meters, no allocation
epics.summary: xj-dsp reproduces the Java mixer where it was good and corrects it where it was not: a fixed voice pool with the quarter-sine release, ten buses allocated up front plus master, the logarithmic DRC and look-ahead compressor ported with their unity default documented, high-pass and low-pass that never existed in Java, a true-peak limiter the Java mixer lacked (16-bit conversion wrapped above 1.0), meters, and a harness proving the callback never allocates or locks.
epics.exit: The graph renders the DemoIT fixtures within tolerance, the callback is proven allocation-free under a counting allocator, and master true peak stays at or below -1 dBTP over an hour of render.

epics.title: Add the insert effects and the device, WAV and null sinks, and prove real-time safety
epics.summary: The per-bus insert chain for gestures (state-variable filter, tempo-synced delay, short reverb, saturator), the cpal device sink across the supported backends, a segmented WAV capture sink (hound caps a WAV at 4 GiB, so an 8-hour capture must be split at musical boundaries), the null sink for faster-than-real-time rendering, and golden render tests against the Java DemoIT fixtures.
epics.exit: Audio plays through CoreAudio, WASAPI and PipeWire with device-loss recovery; an 8-hour capture produces a valid set of boundary-aligned WAVs; golden renders match within tolerance.

epics.title: Build xj-control: inputs, mapping file, cue and gesture routing, moves, LEDs, influence
epics.summary: Turns MIDI, OSC, keyboard and gamepad into cues (to the engine via the station) or gestures (to the DSP), against a TOML profile whose match key is what midir can actually provide, with learn mode in the CLI, LED feedback for the two reference controllers, moves with relative timing, MIDI clock out, and the bounded influence signals.
epics.exit: A MIDI controller drives every cue and gesture from the CLI with LEDs reflecting off/available/armed/active; profiles survive replug on all three OS; moves and influence are replayable from logs.

epics.title: Compose the headless xj-station runtime and CLI: play, render, capture, replay
epics.summary: The control thread that ties engine, transport, DSP, content and control together at 10 to 20 Hz, publishes snapshots, and runs as a CLI. `xj-station play` is the first thing in V2 that makes music (R1); `capture` and `replay` prove determinism end to end; the latency measurement puts numbers on R3. The station also owns the tempo seam: whichever BeatClock is active either feeds the engine's External tempo policy or is driven by the engine's segment tempo.
epics.exit: `xj-station play` on a V1 demo with a MIDI controller makes music; `replay` of a capture reproduces its chain byte for byte; gesture-to-audible at 256 frames is measured and published per platform against the unrelaxed 10 ms budget, with quantized gestures within one frame of the beat and cues at their boundary.

epics.title: Prove the station core in CI: render statistics, an 8-hour soak, and the Phase 2 gate
epics.summary: The Phase 2 exit is measured, not asserted: CI renders demos and checks audio statistics, a nightly soak runs eight hours without dropout, and the maintainers hold the A/B listening gate that decides whether the DSP needs another phase before any UI work.
epics.exit: Nightly soak reports zero dropouts, late commands and xruns; the A/B decision record exists.

epics.title: Ship CLI releases on every tag so the desktop app inherits the pipeline; archive HLS
epics.summary: R1 wants a CLI that makes music before any UI, and 09 Principle 2 wants Build for engine in the first Rust release. Release the xj-station CLI on three OS per tag with checksums and notices so Phase 3 only adds signing, notarization and bundles (R13) to a working workflow. Also archives the HLS design per Q9 while the sinks are fresh.
epics.exit: A tagged commit produces CLI archives for three OS with checksums; the HLS note is in the repository.

epics.title: Build the application shell in the chosen toolkit around the station core
epics.summary: The desktop app is xj-station plus a UI: a shell with Play, Make and Ship modes and settings, the station embedded with its snapshot stream, the canvas-rendered surface component drawn from a view-model (so re-hosting is a UI rewrite), and the 60 fps benchmark on a 2019 laptop; keyboard and screen-reader accessibility of the surface lives in e3-surface, since it waits for every surface element.
epics.exit: The shell opens in under 2 s, embeds a running station, draws the surface component at a sustained 60 fps with meters and 200 timeline elements on a 2019 laptop.

epics.title: Build the performance surface: scenes, palettes, intensity, harmony, layers, transport
epics.summary: Every element of 05-workstation's surface including transport and the on-screen home of every 08 gesture, each tied to a cue or gesture, and each showing what it will do and when before it is touched: previews from the engine, landing times from `earliest_landing`, the commit-horizon line on the harmony strip; and the whole surface drivable from a laptop keyboard with screen-reader labels, built once every element exists.
epics.exit: A musician can perform with the mouse or keyboard: scene and palette cues land where the strip says, the chord picker sends canonical chords, layer strips mute both the bus and future craft, and capture records the set.

epics.title: Build the timeline, the why panel and the diagnostics view
epics.summary: The Java fabrication tab's segment view extended with pending-cue landing points, plus the genuinely new data: the why panel over the engine's choice diagnostics, and a view of messages, craft timing and late counters so the machine is legible (G12).
epics.exit: Clicking any choice shows its candidates, weights and exclusions; the timeline shows where pending cues will land; warnings and timing are visible without a terminal.

epics.title: Build the controller mapping UI with learn mode, LED preview and a moves editor
epics.summary: Plugging in a controller offers a default layout; learn mode writes the TOML; unresolved names are flagged; moves are composed on screen. Reuses the xj-control engine so the CLI and the app share profiles.
epics.exit: A pad controller is mapped to the whole surface in minutes without editing TOML by hand, and LEDs mirror the screen.

epics.title: Make first launch sound in under 10 seconds on a 2019 laptop with a tour
epics.summary: The vision's 'out of the box it makes music': an interim starter bundled as a V1 project (a V1 project is a pack with an implicit manifest; the commissioned CC0 pack arrives in Phase 4), a measured launch-to-sound pipeline, and the three-step tour.
epics.exit: Launch to sound under 10 s on a 2019 laptop is measured and repeatable; a new user completes the tour and is performing.

epics.title: Build Ship mode: Build for engine, bounce, capture export
epics.summary: Game-audio continuity from the first Rust release (09-roadmap principle 2): Build for engine writes exactly what Unreal reads, bounce renders offline, capture export packages a performance with credits.
epics.exit: A game composer builds for Unreal from the Rust workstation on day one; a performance exports as audio plus data with CREDITS.md.

epics.title: Package, sign, notarize and auto-update release-candidate bundles on three platforms
epics.summary: R13 made concrete: bundles per platform from the Phase 2 signing pipeline, an updater configured against the 2026 advisories, and opt-in crash reporting that disables sentry's default usage features; the bundles are the release candidates the usability sessions run on, and the 2.0.0 release itself is e3-release.
epics.exit: Signed, notarized release-candidate bundles install on macOS 12+, Windows 10 21H2+ and Linux glibc 2.35+, update themselves from a signed manifest, and send nothing unless the user opts in.

epics.title: Release Workstation 2.0.0 after the usability gate and turn on licensed official builds
epics.summary: The end of Phase 3 as its own parent issue: Workstation 2.0.0 cut from the signed pipeline once the usability gate records a go, the two consumers of the week-one paperwork that turn `link` and `asio` on in official builds when the grants are on file, and the Windows-on-ARM clause of Q10 closed once a machine exists. Kept apart from e3-packaging so the release-candidate bundles the usability sessions run on are not downstream of the gate those sessions decide.
epics.exit: Workstation 2.0.0 is released from the signed pipeline after the usability gate; `link` and `asio` are on in official builds once their grants are on file; the Windows-on-ARM decision is recorded in the Q10 ADR.

epics.title: Run the usability program that is the Phase 3 exit and gate
epics.summary: R3 is judged by musicians, not by engineers: five sessions with people new to XJ performing with a pad controller after the tour, findings filed as issues, and the gate decision on whether musicians want to play it and what that means for Phase 5 and Phase 6.
epics.exit: Five sessions run, their findings filed as issues, and the post-Phase-3 decision record written.

epics.title: Write the Play-mode and Ship-mode guides, the installation pages and the mapping reference
epics.summary: The docs site gains the performer's guide to the surface, cues, gestures and moves, a reference for the mapping TOML and the two default profiles, and the installation and Ship-mode pages that replace the Java 1.9.x installer and menu-bar pages for 2.0.0 (Play and Ship ship; the editor pages stay for 1.9.x).
epics.exit: docs.xjmusic.com has 2.0.0 installation pages, a Play-mode guide, a Ship-mode guide and a mapping reference matching the 2.0.0 release.

epics.title: Define the pack, show and lockfile formats with content-addressed audio
epics.summary: The shared drive rebuilt as formats: pack.toml and the .xjpack layout with BLAKE3-named audio and a format sidecar (the JSON stores no sample rate, bit depth or channel count), provenance fields, dependency and duplicate-id precedence, the V1 project as a pack with an implicit manifest, and show.toml plus show.lock.
epics.exit: A V1 project and an .xjpack open identically; manifests, shows and lockfiles validate against published schemas; audio is addressed by hash so the demo key collisions that destroyed two samples cannot recur.

epics.title: Ship the xj-content CLI: pack, lint, verify, publish, fetch, lock, render
epics.summary: Every command of 06-commons' tooling table, with the quality bar implemented as lint rules grounded in what the demos actually contain: structural checks, the musical rules (note coverage, loop length within 1 percent with a diagnosis, taxonomy drift, chord grammar), a loudness rule measured with ebur128 on the effective level and calibrated against the demos, and the ten-minute render check.
epics.exit: Every CLI command works end to end against the registry; `xj-content lint` fails the demos exactly where the maps predict and passes the corrected seed packs.

epics.title: Stand up the registry: index repository, artifact bucket and signing keys
epics.summary: Q7 closed on a git index plus Cloudflare R2; this epic creates the xjmusic/commons repository with its static JSON tree, the hash-addressed bucket behind a custom domain, and the minisign-style key scheme kept on a separate pin from the app updater.
epics.exit: The index serves `/index/<name>.json` with no account; artifacts resolve by hash; keys are generated, recorded and verifiable.

epics.title: Run publishing through CI, document authoring, and land an external pack
epics.summary: Publishing is a pull request: CI verifies the signature, lints, renders the preview, uploads the artifact and only then merges the index entry. The authoring guide is written, and the exit demonstration is an outside contributor's pack passing lint. (Mirror and offline fetch tests live with the show loading task in e4-shows.)
epics.exit: One external contributor publishes a pack that passes lint through the PR flow.

epics.title: Make shows load byte-identical content on every station
epics.summary: A show's template taxonomy is the union of its packs' declared categories, emitted in the engine's structured form; the lockfile pins every pack; two machines with the same lock load identical content.
epics.exit: Two CI machines with the same show.lock produce identical content hashes and template configs; the taxonomy union drives the palette rows.

epics.title: Publish xj-base@1, clear the licensing text with counsel, and generate credits
epics.summary: The versioned convention document the manifests cite, counsel's review of the contributor declaration and the CC BY/CC0 interplay with the software license's input-rights clause (Q6's remaining item), and the CREDITS.md generator that makes attribution automatic in every capture, bounce, build and exported pack.
epics.exit: xj-base@1 is published and cited; counsel's wording is adopted; every output carries CREDITS.md.

epics.title: Clear, correct and publish the four demos as packs and commission the starter pack
epics.summary: The demos are known to sound good (R4), but they carry no content license, two samples were destroyed by key collisions, 35 loop audios have wrong metadata, and one palette is declared but unused. Clear the rights, recover the bytes from the CDN, fix what lint finds, publish four packs with previews, commission the CC0 starter pack, and have maintainers listen.
epics.exit: Four demo packs and the starter pack pass lint, have previews, and are approved by two maintainers; the CDN demo export is marked legacy.

epics.title: Bring the Commons into the workstation: browse, fetch, license display, export pack, 2.1
epics.summary: The workstation gains a pack browser and show fetch with offline status, shows the license before a pack is added, exports packs from Ship mode, swaps the interim starter for the commissioned pack, and ships as 2.1.
epics.exit: Workstation 2.1 fetches a show from the registry, shows licenses, exports a lint-passing pack and launches on the CC0 starter pack.

epics.title: Publish the versioned session protocol with conformance fixtures
epics.summary: The third contract: JSON Schema for the fourteen message types with the epoch design from Phase 0, versioned and published so a lighting desk or Max patch can read the harmonic timeline, with fixtures and a reference reader.
epics.exit: The schema is published with a version; a non-XJ reader parses the fixtures.

epics.title: Build xj-session discovery, connection and membership
epics.summary: mDNS discovery with a join code and a manual-IP fallback, QUIC with self-signed certificates bound to the join code (TCP fallback), length-prefixed JSON framing, and the hello/welcome/reject handshake that enforces version and show-lock agreement; presence and clean departure with timeouts.
epics.exit: A follower discovers, joins with a code, is rejected on a lock mismatch, and is timed out cleanly when it vanishes, all under the simulated-network harness.

epics.title: Share the foundation: publish, retract, horizon, claims, cue requests, handoff, failures
epics.summary: The musical heart of the session: the conductor publishes foundation records with sequence numbers and retracts on rewrite, the effective commit horizon is computed from every follower's dub-ahead, layer claims drive Layer Mute cues and bus mutes on every other station, followers' foundation cues become cue requests under the Q13 policy, the conductor role hands off in three steps at a segment boundary, and every row of the failure table has a defined behavior.
epics.exit: In the in-memory and lossy harnesses, two stations hold identical foundations through cues, retracts, claims, handoffs and the full failure table.

epics.title: Add the session BeatClock, the Link epoch mapping and the simulated-network harness
epics.summary: The conductor-hosted clock that works without Link (and is what CI runs on), the bar-identity epoch mapping for Link rooms, the one legitimate use of force_beat_at_time: bridging the session clock into Link for external gear, and the simulated-network transport (latency, jitter, loss, reordering) that the foundation, horizon and failure-table tasks test on before any soak.
epics.exit: Three stations keep beat phase on the session clock within the measured tolerance over the lossy harness; in a Link room followers map the conductor's bars onto their local Link beats without re-anchoring Link.

epics.title: Build the session panel, claim and horizon indicators, and the headless web status page
epics.summary: The session made visible: join code and roles, members and presence, claims on the layer strips, the effective horizon on the harmony strip, cue requests with their senders and collisions, the wired-network recommendation, and a web status page for a headless station in a rack.
epics.exit: A performer joins, claims, requests cues and hands off from the surface; a headless station shows its state in a browser.

epics.title: Soak sessions: handoffs for an hour, three stations for eight, and play the real duet
epics.summary: R15 in order, on the simulated-network harness from e5-session-clock: the one-hour handoff soak, the eight-hour three-station soak with one headless container, and the test that matters: two workstations and an MPC on Link in one room for a 30-minute duet with two handoffs, captured on both stations.
epics.exit: Zero late records on the wired soak, bounded late records on the lossy simulation, and a published duet recording from two captures.

epics.title: Clear the legal review, write the venue guide, hold the post-duet gate, release 2.2
epics.summary: R11: counsel confirms that a paid live performance is 'output audio' under the software license and what the patent license means for a venue running many stations, before 2.2 ships; the venue setup guide is written from the failure table and the soak findings; the gate decides whether Phase 7 is scheduled and whether Q13's default moves; then workstation 2.2 is released.
epics.exit: Counsel's written position is filed and reflected in the license page; the venue guide is published; the post-Phase-5 decision record exists; workstation-v2.2.0 is tagged.

epics.title: Build the editing infrastructure the Rust editors share
epics.summary: Undo and redo (which the Java workstation never had), a content CRUD service with cascades, confirmations and hash-based dirtiness, the library browser with create, duplicate, move and delete, config editors that validate against the C++ parser dialect, and meme entry with suggestions.
epics.exit: Every shared operation from the Java inventory (browser, Cmd modal, config popups, memes container) has a Rust equivalent with undo.

epics.title: Build the instrument and audio editor first, because packs need it
epics.summary: Every operation of the Java instrument and audio editors plus what pack authors need: import of any symphonia-decodable format (the Java dialog offered MP3, AAC and FLAC and then failed on them), a waveform with transient and loop markers, loopBeats proposed from the file length for Loop-mode instruments so the inherited 4.0 default stops producing bad loops, the new pitch-shift and stretch allowances, audition playback of originals and variants, inline lint, and batch processing.
epics.exit: A pack author imports, tags, marks, auditions and lint-checks an instrument without the Java workstation (no destructive trimming: 01's non-goal excludes editing audio; the lint's 'else trim' diagnosis points at an external editor).

epics.title: Build the template editor
epics.summary: Bindings, taxonomy, intensity layers and thresholds, mixer settings, the new commit horizon and hold settings, and template export, with the show's taxonomy union shown when the project is a show.
epics.exit: Every Java template operation has a Rust equivalent, including add-binding with duplicate detection and export.

epics.title: Build the program editor in bind, chord and event modes
epics.summary: The largest editor and most of Phase 6: the program shell with its destructive type cascade and sequence management, bind mode across offsets, chord edit mode with voicing lanes, event edit mode with voices, tracks, patterns and draggable events, and the productivity features the Java editor lacked (multi-select, copy and paste, drag reorder).
epics.exit: Every Java program-editor operation has a Rust equivalent; the Java workstation is no longer the program editor of record.

epics.title: Audit parity, run pack-author sessions, write the migration guide, archive Java
epics.summary: The Phase 6 exit: every Java editing operation checked off against its Rust equivalent, pack authors confirm they can work without Java (R4), the migration guide is written, the round-trip CI is retired, and the Java folder is archived with a pointer.
epics.exit: The parity checklist is complete, the migration guide is published, and workstation/ is archived with a pointer in the repository.

epics.title: Produce the show: a real night, three or more stations, outside artists, a recording
epics.summary: Not an engineering phase. A venue, a date, a network kit, artists who did not build the software, rehearsal, the night, and a recording that stands beside Live in Boulder.
epics.exit: The show happened with three or more stations and outside artists; the recording is published with credits; the retrospective is recorded.

tasks.summary: Submit the signed Steinberg ASIO SDK proprietary agreement (email to reception@steinberg.de, cc info@) per paperwork/steinberg-asio-agreement.md. tasks.summary: xjmusic-demos/LICENSE.txt is the software license plus EULA; it says nothing about redistributing the samples themselves, and some waveform keys suggest third-party sample-library sources. Walk the 3,000 audios' names and the demos' README with the demos' author, classify each instrument's provenance (original, licensed-library, or provenance-to-confirm), and write the question the company and counsel must answer before any demo becomes a CC BY 4.0 or CC0 pack. tasks.title: Create the decision-record convention and record Q7, Q8, Q9, Q13, Q14 and four deferrals
tasks.summary: Create design/v2-proposal/decisions/ with a numbered, dated ADR template (context, options, decision, consequences, evidence) and an index that maps each Q1 to Q14 and each gate to a record. tasks.title: Record the company decisions on Q5 equity, Q6 license, Q11 telemetry and Q12 name
tasks.summary: Put the four yes-or-no questions to the company with the recommended defaults from 11-resolutions: content contributions earn equity on the same PR-based evidence (Q5); CC BY 4.0 default with CC0 starter pack (Q6, pending counsel wording in Phase 4); no usage telemetry, opt-in crash reports, local diagnostics bundle (Q11); one product name, modes Play/Make/Ship, runtime 'XJ station', 'session', 'the Commons' (Q12). tasks.title: Record platform floors and correct the audio-backend promises against cpal 0.18
tasks.summary: Record Q10: macOS 12+ universal, Windows 10 21H2+ x64, Linux glibc 2.35+ x86_64, no 32-bit, no mobile. Correct two statements the research disproved: cpal 0.18.2 has no WASAPI exclusive mode (PR #1368 postponed, v0.19 unscheduled), so 'WASAPI exclusive as an option' is either dropped or scoped as a later fork; and cpal 0.18 ships native PipeWire and PulseAudio hosts with PipeWire the Linux default, replacing the 'JACK or ALSA shims' wording; record the Linux tiers explicitly, since 05 promises 'ALSA and JACK out of the box' and Q10's row lists ALSA direct and JACK: PipeWire is the supported host, JACK (cpal's `jack` feature, built into official Linux binaries) and ALSA direct are best-effort hosts selectable in the station settings, and the real-device overnight run covers PipeWire only. Also record that `realtime` thread promotion on Linux needs CAP_SYS_NICE or rtprio.

tasks.title: Decide which 1.9.6 behaviors are the reference where the C++ port diverged from Java
tasks.summary: 04-engine §5 promises 'behavior-preserving by default', but the map of port regressions shows eleven C++-only or regressed behaviors (persistence window stored as micros, delta never advancing so intensity is pinned at 0.2, store put never overwriting, mute probability throwing at 1.0, delta-arc defects, UB sort comparator) and four inherited quirks. Record the ruling: Java 1.x craft is the reference where the port diverged (rows 1, 2, 2b, 4, 7, 8c, 9a-c, 10) and the common behavior otherwise (rows 5, 6, 8, 8b, 11, 12, 15); add row 16, craft candidate scope (C++ phase 2 of chooseFreshProgram/chooseFreshInstrument draws from every Published entity in projectContent, while the Java workstation handed the engine the forTemplate subset, so the Unreal plugin today can pick from unbound libraries) and rule for the Java reference as a create-time setting: the C++ seconds-taking constructor defaults to the 1.9.6 behavior so Unreal hosts do not change, the ABI defaults to the Java forTemplate behavior; decide 2c (two-decimal intensity floor), 5 (dub intensity from the segment spanning `at` versus Java's one-segment lag from segments.at(0)) and 8c ('BIG' vs 'LARGE' event label) explicitly because they change golden values. The in-tree timing harness dump is the runtime evidence for row 2.

tasks.title: Decide where V2 additive content fields live while the Java workstation still saves
tasks.summary: Jackson is configured FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=false and both config formatters emit only known keys, so any V2 field (allowPitchShift, pitchShiftRange, allowStretch, contentHash, originPack, originVersion, commitHorizonBeats, followHoldMaxBars) written into the shared JSON is erased by the next Java save. A sidecar cannot live inside the entity trees: ProjectManagerImpl.saveProjectContent deletes every file under libraries/, templates/ and instrument/ it did not just rewrite, and the Java opener globs libraries/**/*.json and templates/**/*.json as HubContent, so a `<name>.v2.json` there is ingested as empty content and then erased on save. Record the choice: one sidecar outside the swept trees and outside the Java globs (`<Project>.v2.json` beside the `.xj`, or a top-level `v2/` folder keyed by entity id) owned by xj-content during the transition, merged on read by entity UUID with the sidecar winning for V2 fields and dropping entries whose UUID no longer exists, with the Java-era files untouched; the only alternative is accepting loss until the Phase 6 archive. Name the merge rule and the removal date.

tasks.title: Decide per-component release tags so engine 2.0.0 ships beside the Java 1.9.x line
tasks.summary: engine_distro.yml and workstation_distro.yml fire on every tag and fail unless workstation/gradle.properties, engine/CMakeLists.txt VERSION and the tag agree, which makes 09-roadmap's version plan impossible. Record the scheme: `engine-v2.0.0` (with the C ABI version in the release notes), `workstation-v2.x` for the Rust workstation with `workstation-v2.0.0-alpha.N` pre-release tags for the Phase 2 xj-station CLI releases (so the stable 2.0 line is not consumed before Phase 3), `v1.9.x` kept for the Java workstation, and the Unreal plugin's existing `<plugin>-<engine>` convention. Phase 1 rewrites the verify jobs against this record.

tasks.title: Hold the Phase 0 gate: toolkit, stretch library, Link path, go/no-go on the plan
tasks.summary: Convene the gate when every spike row has a recorded decision. Confirm the toolkit (Q1), stretch library (Q2) and Link path (Q3 default: BeatClock trait with `link` and `session` implementations, license pending) records, the 2019-laptop craft measurement, the taxonomy review and the C ABI spike report, and record the go/no-go on the plan as a whole with the Phase 1 and Phase 2 start order for a single engineer (R10).

tasks.title: Amend the proposal chapters with the Phase 0 corrections and cite each decision record
tasks.summary: Keep the folder the single description of the plan: fix 05's cpal/midir/Link rows (no WASAPI exclusive in cpal 0.18, native PipeWire, no manufacturer/product or hot-plug in midir), 08's `match` example to the port-name glob plus inquiry key, 02/04's generator count (seven sites, not four), 02/06's 'cloned from git' (demos are fetched from audio.xj.io), 02's claim that the example app plays audio, 07's epoch wording (bar identity plus conductor clock micros) the ASIO turnaround estimate, Q14's barBeats filter wording (Beat and Detail programs only; Transition and Background choose instruments), each section citing its ADR. Also correct 09's dependency diagram: Export pack and 2.1 need the Phase 3 shell (P3 to P4) and the hello handshake needs show.lock (P4 to P5), so Phase 4 cannot finish before Phase 3's shell exists.

tasks.title: Add a minimal xjmusic_c CMake target with install rule and gate the example app
tasks.summary: engine/CMakeLists.txt declares LANGUAGES CXX only, has no install() or export anywhere, and adds example/ unconditionally so every consumer configures SDL2 from a vendored tarball. Add enable_language(C), a throwaway `xjmusic_c` target exposing create/start/run_cycle/finish behind extern "C", CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON, an install() rule, and an XJ_BUILD_EXAMPLE option defaulting OFF when not top-level. Done when `cmake --install` produces a header plus static archive on all three platforms.

tasks.title: Write the Rust spike that links the engine from build.rs, plays via cpal, and report it
tasks.summary: A single-crate Rust program whose build.rs drives cmake (the `cmake` crate) to build the spike target and links it statically, with bindgen (libclang) over the throwaway header. It loads engine/test/_data/test_project, calls run_cycle at a 100 ms tick, decodes the build/*.wav files with hound and plays scheduled audio through cpal 0.18 (streams must be `play()`ed explicitly). Add a GitHub Actions job that builds and runs it with a null device on ubuntu-latest, macos-14 and windows-latest; done when all three are green. Close with the spike report that seeds xj-engine-sys: libclang availability per runner, MSVC CRT versus the engine's Debug/Release config, whether PIC is needed on Linux, static-link order, and which Engine members could not be expressed in flat C (std::string ids, raw pointers in AudioScheduleEvent).

tasks.title: Check in the craft-timing harness as an engine target with a per-segment delta dump
tasks.summary: Move design/v2-proposal/tools/craft_timing.cpp into engine/bench as a CMake target built with Release flags, driving Engine::RunCycle at a 100 ms simulated tick on the test project and the checked-in demo build payloads. Add the six-line per-segment print of id, type, delta, total and intensity so the delta-never-advances regression (delta stays 0, intensity 0.200 on every segment) is observed at runtime rather than inferred. Print inside the loop whenever the segment count changes, since the 3.6 ms persistence window deletes earlier segments.

tasks.title: Measure craft, rewrite and load timing on a 2019 laptop and the largest content
tasks.summary: Run the harness on a 2019 Intel MacBook (and one Windows laptop of similar age) with default and Play-mode horizons on the checked-in Deep House payload (the largest demo; craft timing needs no audio) with a macro override every 20 s. Record mean/p95/p99/max per cycle class (the per-stage split is added in Phase 1 when the timing messages exist). Decide, in a decision record, whether the inline-craft design holds (the proposal retires the craft-on-another-thread contingency unless this contradicts it by an order of magnitude).

tasks.title: Check in the four demo build payloads as JSON-only engine fixtures from xjmusic-demos
tasks.summary: xjmusic-demos commits no build/ folder and the engine reads only `.xj` plus `build/**/*.json`, yet the timing harness, the compatibility fixture and the fuzz corpus all want 'the demo build payloads'. Write a script that merges each demo's libraries/ and templates/ JSON into one HubContent-shaped `build/<slug>.json` exactly as the Java Build does for the JSON half (orphans removed, waveformKey rewritten to `<audioId>.ext`), with no audio, and check the four files (about 4 MB) into engine/test/_data/demos/ with the script and the demos commit hash recorded; a test loads each through the path loader. Done when the harness and the compatibility fixture run on them in CI without any audio present.

tasks.title: Define the surface view-model snapshot and a fake station stream for both toolkit slices
tasks.summary: A small Rust crate that emits the snapshot shape the surface will consume: scenes (macro names), palette rows, a harmony strip with chords and a moving commit-horizon line, ten layer meters updated at 60 Hz, and 200 timeline elements scrolling. It is the view-model contract that makes the surface portable between hosts (R2 mitigation) and is reused by the Phase 3 canvas component tests. It may also take the Rust spike player as a live source when that spike is available, without the UI spike waiting for it.

tasks.title: Build the Tauri 2 + Svelte slice with a Canvas2D surface on Windows, macOS and Linux
tasks.summary: Candidate A on tauri 2.12 (MSRV 1.90): the shell in Svelte, the surface drawn on a Canvas2D component (WebGPU is absent in WebKitGTK and only on by default in WKWebView from macOS 26, so Canvas2D or WebGL2 is the portable path), fed by the fixture through Tauri commands or a channel. Measure sustained fps with meters, animated chord strip and 200 timeline elements on a 2019 laptop, time to window, Linux webkit2gtk behavior, and note the updater/bundler story.

tasks.title: Build the iced slice with a wgpu surface on Windows, macOS and Linux
tasks.summary: Candidate B1 on iced 0.14 (MSRV 1.88; master needs 1.93 and a winit fork): the same slice drawn through a custom wgpu widget with the tiny-skia fallback checked. Measure the same criteria; record the accessibility status (issue #552 open since 2019, no AccessKit), the bundler story (cargo-packager dormant since 2025-11), and the wgpu major-version churn the surface would track.

tasks.title: Score both slices against the eight criteria and record the Q1 toolkit decision
tasks.summary: Score criteria 1 to 8 (60 fps on a 2019 laptop, visual ceiling, time to first sound under 2 s, iteration speed, accessibility, cross-platform parity, contributor pool, no separate Linux path) for both candidates with measurements attached. Record in the Q1 ADR that both slices were driven by the fake snapshot stream rather than a running engine, and restate criterion 3 as window-to-first-frame of the surface under 2 s here plus the Phase 3 launch-to-sound target measured on the real pipeline. Apply the tie-breaker (Candidate A) only if the scores tie; record the decision and the condition under which the surface would be scoped down (both miss 60 fps).

tasks.title: Assemble the fixed bake-off material and render it with Signalsmith Stretch and Bungee
tasks.summary: Collect rights-clear material per 11-resolutions Q2: four drum loops, four sustained pads, four bass samples, four vocal-like samples, each rendered at 0.93x and 1.07x stretch and at plus or minus 2 and 4 semitones. Render set A with Signalsmith Stretch 1.3.2 compiled from upstream via `cc` (the signalsmith-stretch 0.1.3 crate pins a June 2025 commit) and set B with a small C++ driver over Bungee v2.4.35's granular API (bungee-rs is archived). Randomize and label the files for blind listening.

tasks.title: Hold the blind listening session and record the Q2 stretch-library decision
tasks.summary: Three musicians listen blind and score transient preservation, phase coherence, low-frequency smearing and formant behavior per sample class. Record the decision (default Signalsmith unless Bungee wins clearly), the license consequence (MPL file-level copyleft for Bungee), and reaffirm the architecture: variants are rendered ahead of time on the I/O thread, never on the audio thread, so the choice does not touch the DSP voice model.

tasks.title: Demonstrate a Rust process locking tempo and phase with an MPC and Ableton Live on a LAN
tasks.summary: Run rusty_link 0.4.9 as published (it vendors Link 4.0.0b3; GPL-2.0-or-later, used only for internal, non-distributed prototyping on company machines while the license request is open, which question 5 of the request asks Ableton to confirm) against an MPC One and Ableton Live on a wired switch and on Wi-Fi: tempo changes from any peer propagate (TEST-PLAN TEMPO-1), joining does not disturb existing peers (BEATTIME-2), enable/disable causes no beat jump (BEATTIME-1), and start/stop sync is left off. Capture the wire traffic to explain whether the LinkAudio-disabled 4.0.0b3 instance interoperates with the MPC's Link implementation (its Link and protocol version recorded as a finding), and record peer counts, convergence time, any phase jump at join, and the cross-device click offset against the MPC metronome.

tasks.title: Measure beat-to-DAC alignment under 3 ms per audio host and map cpal instants to Link time
tasks.summary: Link's TEST-PLAN AUDIOENGINE-1 requires a click rendered at beat_at(DAC time) to align with LinkHut within 3 ms. Build the loopback rig on CoreAudio, WASAPI shared and PipeWire/ALSA using cpal 0.18 timestamps: on macOS and WASAPI the StreamInstant shares Link's clock base, on ALSA/JACK/PipeWire it does not, so measure the per-stream regression (512-point HostTimeFilter) path too. Record per-host output-latency offsets (cpal's CoreAudio `playback` adds buffer plus latency plus safety offset while Link adds only kAudioDevicePropertyLatency) and the need for a per-device trim setting.

tasks.title: Record the session epoch design and the Link-path decision
tasks.summary: Link shares phase, tempo and optionally the transport instant; beat magnitude is per instance and a joiner's beat_at jumps by up to half a quantum, so the epoch cannot be '(T0, B0) in Link beats'. Record option 2 from the gap map: `welcome` and every foundation record carry the conductor's bar identity plus the conductor's Link-clock micros at that downbeat; followers translate with the NTP-style offset the `session` clock needs anyway and snap to the nearest grid downbeat with beat_at/time_at_beat under one pinned snap quantum (barBeats only for phase display); `force_beat_at_time` is reserved for the session-to-Link bridge. Also record: start/stop sync off by default, a pinned snap quantum rather than quantum equals barBeats, BeatClock has `link` and `session` implementations behind feature flags, and the proprietary-license fallback. Record too the Link version pin (Ableton/link 4.1.1) and the plan to fork the binding in Phase 2 under the XJ workspace, since rusty_link is a one-person project last touched 2026-01; Ableton's grant can cover only Link and abl_link, so shipping the binding also needs its author's relicense or an XJ-written binding over abl_link.h.

tasks.title: Draft the xj-base@1 convention document from the demo analysis
tasks.summary: Write the short conventions document from 11-resolutions Q4: NNNBPM recorded tempo, NNOTE voicing density, SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE size aligned with eventNamesSmall/Medium/Large, BREAK/INTRO/OUTRO structure on bindings, the open character list (OPEN, WIDEOPEN, STRAIGHT, ROOTSY), and the meme grammar as implemented (!X anti, X! strong, $X unique, numeric prefix exclusive). State the engine constraint that taxonomy categories are sanitized to letters only (digits, ! and $ stripped), so conventions live outside the taxonomy and are enforced by MemeStack, and reserve a section for the loudness rule.

tasks.title: Review xj-base@1 with the first pack authors and record the Q4 decision
tasks.summary: Walk the draft with the people who will author the first packs (the demo authors and at least one outside musician): the convention list, the character memes, the per-pack declared palettes in `CATEGORY[A, B, C]` syntax, and the lint drift rules. Amend, and record the Q4 decision with the agreed list and the revision trigger in Phase 4.

tasks.title: Measure loudness and true peak of the 3,000 demo audios to calibrate the level rule
tasks.summary: Before xj-base@1 freezes a level target, measure every demo WAV (fetched from audio.xj.io, since the repo audio is not local) with the `ebur128` crate: integrated loudness for sustained audio (Loop mode or at least 3 s), max momentary loudness for one-shots (zero-padded under 400 ms), and true peak, in the playback channel layout and at the effective level (file plus 20·log10(audio.volume × instrument.volume)). Publish the distribution per demo and per instrument mode; the lint's -18 LUFS ±3 LU proposal is adopted or replaced by the demo median rounded to the nearest LU.

tasks.title: Enumerate both reference controllers through midir on three OS and prove the match key
tasks.summary: midir 0.11.1 exposes only `id()` (ALSA 'client:port' address, CoreMIDI uniqueID, WinMM device-interface path) and `port_name()`; no manufacturer, product or VID:PID. Enumerate a Launchpad Mini MK3 and an MPD218 on Linux, macOS and Windows, record every string including the 31-char ALSA truncation and the Windows 'MIDIIN2 (...)' prefix, and send a Universal Device Inquiry (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7) on each port to prove the port-name glob plus inquiry-reply key works everywhere. Record that `id()` must never be the persisted profile binding.

tasks.title: Verify Launchpad Programmer-mode and MPD218 LED behavior on hardware
tasks.summary: On the Launchpad Mini MK3 confirm Programmer mode entry (F0 00 20 29 02 0D 0E 01 F7) on the `LPMiniMK3 MIDI` interface, static/flash/pulse on channels 1 to 3, the SysEx batch colourspec form, flash locking to incoming MIDI beat clock, and recovery from a crash that leaves the device in Programmer mode. On the MPD218 verify the factory note table (Bank A channel 10 notes 36 to 51) and that Note On on a pad's own note lights its LED. Capture raw input byte logs (pads, CCs, inquiry replies) per device and OS as fixtures for the Phase 2 profile replay test. These facts and logs become the two default profiles and their CI test.

tasks.title: Create v2 labels, milestones and the project board, and reconcile conflicting issues
tasks.summary: Create labels `v2`, one per area, eighteen in all: the frame's seventeen (engine, c-abi, rust-engine, content, dsp, transport, control, station, session, workstation-ui, commons, ci-release, docs, legal-paperwork, decision, unreal, show) plus commons-content, the one label added beyond the frame for the seed-content epic, milestones per phase with one naming convention, and the 'v2.0 Collaborative Musical Instrument' project (requires `gh auth refresh -s read:project,project`).
