tasks.title: Make segment-store reads address-independent so craft iteration order is stable
tasks.summary: Every `readAll*` on SegmentEntityStore returns `std::set<const T*>` ordered by pointer address, and `selectAudioIntensityLayers` sorts pointer-ordered audio sets by intensity with pointer-order ties (Craft.cpp:405-409), so a seed alone cannot make craft reproducible. Return vectors sorted by (segmentId, id) or sort at every consumer, tie-break the intensity sort by id, and add a test that shuffles allocation order and asserts identical choices. This is the prerequisite the determinism tests need to be meaningful. Also tie-break every craft-path std::sort by id (std::sort is unstable and tie order differs between libstdc++, libc++ and MSVC), and restore Java's most-notes chord de-ghosting, which the port broke with a map emplace (Fabricator.cpp:501), before any golden is captured.

tasks.title: Add JSON serializers for the ten segment entity types with fixed sort keys
tasks.summary: No segment entity has JSON serialization today (only content entities and StickyBun do), yet the determinism golden format, `xj_engine_get_segments_json` and the foundation record all need one. Add `to_json` for Chain, Segment and the eight child types using the existing `toString` enum maps, with a specified sort key per array (choices by id, chords by position, picks by startAtSegmentMicros then id) a determinism mode that omits createdAt/updatedAt wall-clock stamps, and the one explicit no-chord representation (an explicit null for SegmentChord.name, since `NC` has no stable spelling) that the foundation record, the Chord cue and the Rust grammar port all reuse. Reuse the EngineTest::computeKey micros-exact shape for schedule events.

tasks.title: Write the determinism tests and a three-platform craft golden before touching any RNG
tasks.summary: Per R9 the tests exist before the swap. Add gtest cases that run the same project and seed twice over the richer Beat/Detail fixture (so MarbleBag, chooseVoicing, StickyBun and NotePicker are all exercised) and compare sorted store dumps; the scripts drive the existing override API only (the cue API does not exist yet) and contain no overrides that trigger a rewrite or cutoff, because the rewrite arithmetic is unified later in the cue queue and asserted by the cue tests, plus a craft-matrix golden captured per platform; mark them expected-fail against the unseeded engine. Also capture the current random distribution of choices over N runs as a sanity baseline so the swap can show it did not change the distribution. The goldens are captured after every port fix lands (including delta arcs, the comparator and the float-literal rule, which change choice order and loaded tempos), and after the per-engine 128-bit ids, which change every segment-side id in a dump, so they encode the reference behavior in the final id format and are never re-baselined by a fix or by the id change.

tasks.title: Implement engine-owned RNG primitives and the chain seed, test vectors on three toolchains
tasks.summary: `std::uniform_int_distribution`, `uniform_real_distribution` and `std::shuffle` are implementation-defined and differ between libc++, libstdc++ and MSVC, so a shared mt19937_64 seed alone would give different stores per CI runner. Implement `xj::Rng` (mt19937_64) with `bounded(n)` (Lemire multiply-high with rejection, written out), `unit()` and `fisher_yates()`, with golden vectors asserted on all three platforms. Also add the chain seed field, a public documented `XJ::Engine::setSeed(uint64_t)` valid only before start (an error afterwards) and `XJ::Engine::getSeed()` reporting the drawn seed when unset, with the seed drawn once at start; no craft site uses the Rng yet, so this lands before the red determinism tests and the swap PR, which then contains nothing but the generator swap (04 §5, R9).

tasks.title: Thread the engine-owned generator through all seven RNG sites in one PR, nothing else
tasks.summary: The proposal counts four generators; the code has seven construction sites in six files (five components): StickyBun statics, ValueUtils statics, MarbleBag instance plus per-call `quickPick` and `quickBooleanChanceOf`, Craft::gen for shuffles, and the per-call generator in Fabricator::chooseVoicing. Pass the chain's Rng by reference (MarbleBag is value-copied and must not own one), and replace the std distributions with the primitives (the chain seed, its pre-start setter and the drawn-seed report already exist from the primitives task). One PR, nothing else in it; the craft matrix must pass and the red determinism tests turn green.

tasks.title: Make entity ids per engine and 128-bit so two handles in one process never collide
tasks.summary: `EntityUtils::computeUniqueId` is a process-global 12-hex counter shared by every Engine in a process, so two engines in one process (the follow test, the Rust wrapper) issue colliding segment-side ids, and a 16-byte `active_audio_id` cannot be a byte-cast of today's string. Move the counter into the chain and emit 128-bit ids (a prefix drawn from the chain seed (the primitives task's field and setter) through `xj::Rng` at start, plus a per-chain counter) that the ABI returns as byte arrays, so the same seed reproduces the same ids and golden dumps and replays stay byte-identical; this depends on the RNG primitives but not on the swap PR, which separately removes the StickyBun and ValueUtils static generators. Two engines in one process draw different seeds unless told otherwise; across stations, records are identified by the session envelope's sender and seq, not by segment-side ids.

tasks.title: Derive a per-segment sub-seed so a cue rewrite reproduces the same future
tasks.summary: Derive each segment's sub-seed from the chain seed and segment id and re-seed the Rng at segment start, covering MarbleBag, chooseVoicing, StickyBun creation and computeMute. Test: crafting with a cue applied from the start equals rewriting from that cue later. This property is what makes cue tests and preview deterministic.

tasks.title: Compare golden store dumps across the three CI platforms and document the FP caveat
tasks.summary: Build golden store fixtures once and assert them on ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners every PR. Where floating-point fields (intensity, micros arithmetic) differ, exclude or round them and document that determinism is promised per binary and platform, which the session design does not depend on.

tasks.title: Fix the persistence window units together with the dub intensity source
tasks.summary: CraftWork.cpp:28 stores `persistenceWindowSeconds` unconverted as micros, so the window is 3,600 microseconds and audio tails are cut at every segment boundary; fixing it alone makes `segments.at(0)` in DubWork.cpp:112 the previous segment and lags intensity by a segment (Java behavior). Multiply by MICROS_PER_SECOND and take dub intensity from whichever segment the reference-behavior record's row 5 ruling names (the segment spanning `at`, or Java's previous-segment lag). Add the missing test for an audio tail crossing a segment boundary.

tasks.title: Mine the Java craft tests for expectations the C++ matrix lacks before retiring Java
tasks.summary: 03-architecture retires the Java engine only after its tests are mined. Walk io.xj.engine's craft, fabricator and work tests and port every expectation the gtest matrix does not assert (CraftFoundationContinueTest's 0.23 intensity, delta advance, cutoff trimming of straddling picks, store put replacement, the mute roll at probability 1) as new or corrected gtest cases, expected-fail where the port regressed. These are the acceptance tests the fixes turn green.
proposal_refs: 03-architecture.md What happens to each V1 piece

tasks.title: Restore delta accumulation and the intensity crescendo, updating the foundation fixtures
tasks.summary: MacroMainCraft.cpp:81 adds `segment->total` from the shell segment (always 0) and :86 computes intensity from the stale delta, so delta never leaves 0, intensity is pinned at intensityAutoCrescendoMinimum and mainProgramLengthMaxDelta never ends a main program; Java does both correctly. Set total before delta, compute intensity from the new delta, apply or reject the two-decimal floor per the ruling, update CraftFoundationContinueTest (0.2 becomes 0.23) and any delta-dependent fixture, and confirm with the harness dump that delta climbs and intensity rises.

tasks.title: Read ProgramVoice and ProgramVoiceTrack name/order from the right JSON keys, with a test
tasks.summary: ProgramVoice.h:40-41 and ProgramVoiceTrack.h:33-34 read `duration` and `tones` into name and order (copy-pasted from the pattern event), so every voice and track loaded from JSON has an empty name and drum event-to-audio matching (Craft.cpp:960) cannot score. Fix the keys and add a loader fixture containing a Beat program exported by the workstation that asserts track names, since the engine test project has no Beat or Detail programs.

tasks.title: Make child-entity put replace existing ids in the store and in the active-audio diff
tasks.summary: SegmentEntityStore.cpp:16 uses `emplace`, so re-putting a pick (the cutoff trim in doCutoffLastSegment) is silently dropped and tails cross cue boundaries; WorkManager.cpp:86 has the same defect, so an `Update` event is re-emitted every cycle and the eventual `Delete` carries stale values. Switch both to insert_or_assign semantics, state the rule in the store contract, and add tests for cutoff trimming and single-emission of updates. Follow mode and cue rewrites re-put entities for the same segment and depend on this.

tasks.title: Fix the UB comparator, null chain optional, float-literal rule, mute bound, Transition label and intensityLayers load check
tasks.summary: Six small defects the reference ruling assigns here, each with a crash, silent-data or label consequence: WorkManager.cpp:121 returns `compare()` as bool (not a strict weak ordering, UB); readChain returns an engaged optional holding nullptr so both guards are dead; `setIfNotNull(float&)` requires `is_number_float` so `"tempo": 120` reads as 0; `quickBooleanChanceOf` throws for probability >= 1; the Transition pick label is the alphabetically first of `eventNamesLarge/Medium/Small` (a std::set) instead of the first authored name (row 8c); a type missing from `intensityLayers` divides by zero in Craft.cpp:418-424 (row 15). Fix each (strict `<` then id, nullopt, `is_number()`, bound [0,1] with `<` and one draw per call, authored-order vectors beside the membership sets, load-time fallback to the default layer count with a Warning) with a test, including p=1 always mutes and p=0 never mutes.

tasks.title: Repair the three delta-arc defects and give the feature a real test
tasks.summary: Delta arcs are off by default but a 'build' or 'drop return' move would lean on them: Craft.cpp:98 pushes an empty string instead of the layer, Craft.h:93 slices the ChoiceIndexProvider so lookups use key "", and a third shuffle at Craft.cpp:110 defeats deltaArcBeatLayersToPrioritize; CraftTest::PrecomputeDeltas has no assertions. Fix all three, use `std::function` or a pointer for the provider, and write an asserting test (seed-exact once the RNG swap lands) that prioritized layers enter first and deltas stagger by deltaUnits.

tasks.title: Widen every chain-time field to int64 and accept sub-second horizons in settings
tasks.summary: Segment::beginAtChainMicros, pick startAtSegmentMicros/lengthMicros, CraftWork members and ChainUtils use `long` (32-bit on MSVC, so chain time saturates at 35.8 minutes in Windows builds), and WorkSettings takes whole seconds as `int`, so a one-beat commit horizon is unrepresentable. Change all time fields to int64_t, make WorkSettings hold micros with a settings struct the ABI can pass while keeping the seconds-taking C++ constructor overload the Unreal plugin compiles against (Q8: the C++ API stays first-class), and add a test that runs a chain past 36 minutes on Windows.

tasks.title: Build a JSON-loaded test fixture with Beat and Detail programs and event-mode instruments
tasks.summary: The engine test project contains only four macro and four main programs and three loop instruments, so EngineTest never exercises BeatCraft or DetailCraft on disk content. Export a fixture from the workstation (or derive from the checked-in Hero's Journey and Deep House build payloads) with Beat and Detail programs, event-mode instruments with tones, and voicings, loadable from JSON; it is the fixture for the follow-mode, determinism and compatibility tests.

tasks.title: Compile-test every C++ symbol the Unreal plugin uses; pin the Build-for-engine contract
tasks.summary: XjMainEngine.cpp uses a fixed set: the six-argument Engine constructor with optional seconds, start, RunCycle and AudioScheduleEvent accessors, getAllMacroPrograms, doOverrideMemes/Macro, setIntensityOverride, getTemplateContent()->getMemeTaxonomy().getCategories(), getSegmentStore()->readChoice/readAll*, WorkSettings fields and Program::config.barBeats. Add engine/test/compat/unreal_surface.cpp that references each one so a signature change fails the PR. Record as a decision the Build-for-engine contract the plugin depends on: WAV 48 kHz, 16-bit, stereo named `<InstrumentAudio.id>.wav` plus `<slug>.json`, with OGG as a later opt-in (Q8: the plugin stays on the C++ API).

tasks.title: Scope craft candidates to the started template behind a setting defaulting to 1.9.6 on C++
tasks.summary: Row 16 of the reference ruling: C++ phase 2 of chooseFreshProgram/chooseFreshInstrument draws from every Published entity in projectContent, and Fabricator.cpp:37-38 reads every template's bindings, while the Java workstation handed the engine the forTemplate subset. Add a create-time setting `craftCandidateScope` {AllPublished, StartedTemplate}: the seconds-taking C++ constructor the Unreal plugin uses defaults to AllPublished (1.9.6 behavior, so the game-audio product does not change what it can choose), the ABI settings struct defaults to StartedTemplate (the Java reference). Implement the scoping of bindings and phase-2 candidates to the started template's reachable content, with a multi-template fixture test asserting candidates come only from the started template under StartedTemplate and from everything under AllPublished, and the release-note wording for Unreal hosts who want the Java behavior.

tasks.title: Write xj_c.h with the status enum, ABI version, buffer ownership and id conventions
tasks.summary: Author the header skeleton from the contract register: extern "C", opaque `xj_engine*`, `xj_abi_version()` returning 1.0.0, `xj_status` with a code for every failure class including calls before start, UTF-8 strings with explicit length, engine-owned buffers valid until the next call on the handle or `xj_free`, 16-byte UUID arrays, an export-visibility macro header, and the one-handle-one-thread rule in the doc comments. Everything later in the ABI adds to this file.

tasks.title: Implement create, destroy, load from path or JSON, start, finish and the existing controls
tasks.summary: `xj_engine_create` and `xj_engine_destroy` own the handle; create takes settings in micros (sub-second horizons), `xj_engine_load_project` accepts a path or an in-memory JSON payload through a new `Engine::loadProjectContent(json, audioRoot)` (today only the path loader exists and it reads `.xj` plus `build/**/*.json`), `xj_engine_start` clears the segment store as Engine.h:40 already claims and hands the chosen template to CraftWork instead of an arbitrary pointer-ordered one, with the ABI's create settings defaulting `craftCandidateScope` to StartedTemplate (the candidate scoping itself is the port-fixes task's), and `xj_engine_finish` keeps the 1.9.6 contract: it stops crafting and the next `xj_engine_run_cycle` returns the trailing Delete events (engine-api-lifecycle §3), stated in the header doc comments and the host guide rather than adding out-pointers the register does not give it. Add `xj_engine_set_control_mode` (valid only before `xj_engine_start`, returning an `xj_status` error afterwards, because Fabricator::ControlMode is consulted exactly once in WorkManager::start to pre-apply an override; in 2.0 it is a convenience over the Macro/Memes cue path), `xj_engine_override_macro`, `xj_engine_override_memes`, `xj_engine_set_intensity_override`.

tasks.title: Implement xj_engine_run_cycle with the flat xj_schedule_event array and a string table
tasks.summary: Implement `xj_engine_run_cycle(at_chain_micros, out_events, out_count)` returning the register's `xj_schedule_event` struct (type, instrument_type, instrument_mode, ids, start/stop micros, volumes, release, pitch_shift_semitones, stretch_ratio, waveform_key_offset into a string table). Copy values at the boundary before any cleanup, emit events in time order, and document that Delete may revoke audio already playing and that `getPick()` is invalid on a Delete. Pick ids are per-engine 128-bit values, not byte-casts of the 12-hex strings. Content ids are unvalidated strings today: a canonical 36-character UUID is packed as its 16 bytes; any other id string (ContentFixtures and hand-authored projects carry them) is hashed deterministically to 16 bytes with a documented 128-bit FNV-1a and reported as a load warning, so `instrument_audio_id[16]` is always well defined.

tasks.title: Make work failure observable and replace cout/cerr with a host log callback
tasks.summary: `WorkState::Failed` is unreachable because CraftWork catches every exception and simply stops; a host cannot tell 'failed' from 'healthy but silent'. Propagate didFailWhile to a Failed state and an `xj_status`, expose it through `xj_engine_get_work_state`, add `xj_engine_set_log_callback` replacing the std::cout/std::cerr prints, and return structured load errors instead of swallowing them in the build-folder crawl.

tasks.title: Add the xjmusic_c target with install, export, PIC and a generated version header
tasks.summary: Promote the spike's target: `xjmusic_c` compiled into the same static library with the C ABI, `install()` of headers and archive, an export set and package-config so `find_package(xjmusic)` works, CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON, a generated `xj_version.h` with engine and ABI versions, enable_language(C), and `XJ_BUILD_EXAMPLE` off for consumers. Nothing changes for the existing `xjmusic` C++ target that Unreal builds.

tasks.title: Compile a C11 test program against xj_c.h with a C compiler on three platforms in CI
tasks.summary: Write engine/test/c/xj_c_test.c exercising create, load from memory, start, run_cycle, overrides, finish and error returns, compiled as C (not C++) with gcc, clang and cl, linked against the installed archive. Add it to engine_ci and engine_pr on all four runners; this proves the header is actually C.

tasks.title: Run gtest and the C ABI tests under AddressSanitizer and UBSan in CI
tasks.summary: Add a sanitizer configuration (-fsanitize=address,undefined on Linux and macOS; /fsanitize=address on MSVC) that builds the library, xjmusic_test and the C test, runs them from build/test so the relative `_data/` paths resolve, and fails the PR on any report. Fix what it finds (the dangling pick pointers in Delete events are the expected first catch).

tasks.title: Write libFuzzer targets for JSON, cues, foundation records and grammar; run them nightly
tasks.summary: Four targets through the C ABI: content JSON into `xj_engine_load_project` (seeded from the checked-in demo build payloads and test data), random cue sequences against `xj_engine_cue`/`xj_engine_preview_cue_json`/`run_cycle` with the pending-cue queue (the preview runs on every random cue before it is sent, so the scratch copy is fuzzed too), foundation JSON into `xj_engine_push_foundation_json`, and `Chord::of`/`Note::of` on arbitrary strings. Every finding becomes a regression test; this is the ABI-boundary mitigation for R8. A scheduled nightly workflow runs each target for a fixed budget, persists the corpus as an artifact, uploads crashers and opens an issue on a new crash; it is required green for the 2.0.0 tag.

tasks.title: Capture the ABI 1.0.0 baseline and fail PRs that change xj_c.h without a semver bump
tasks.summary: 04-engine §12 says the C ABI follows semver strictly (additive functions bump minor, any change to an existing struct or signature bumps major) but nothing enforced the freeze after engine-v2.0.0. Store the header's declarations (parsed, not textual) and the exported symbol list as a baseline at the tag, diff them on every PR, require a minor bump in the generated version header for additions and a major bump for any changed signature, enum value or struct layout; the Rust-side witness (regenerating and diffing the checked-in bindgen bindings) is a Phase 2 CI task once xj-engine-sys exists. Done when a PR that renames a field fails without a major bump and one that adds a function fails without a minor bump.

tasks.title: Add commitHorizonBeats, followHoldMaxBars and mixerFiltersEnabled to TemplateConfig
tasks.summary: Parse `commitHorizonBeats` (float, default reproducing 1.9.x behavior, i.e. the implicit deadline-derived horizon) `followHoldMaxBars` (int) and `mixerFiltersEnabled` (bool, default false; the new name that lets xj-dsp's master filters be opted into, since the threshold keys are always present) in TemplateConfig.cpp with getters, emit them in `toString()` so the C++ formatter does not drop them, and add ConfigParser tests. Note the parser types by literal shape: `1` is int, `1.0` is float, and the typed getters throw on mismatch.

tasks.title: Define the commit horizon in chain micros and implement exact earliest-landing arithmetic
tasks.summary: Today's de-facto horizon is `deadlineMicros` (1 s) with floor-then-ceil beat arithmetic that can land inside or before the deadline at slow tempos, and three different beats-to-micros formulas (CraftWork.cpp:300, :336, Fabricator.cpp:754). Unify the conversion, derive the horizon from commitHorizonBeats at the current segment tempo, and implement `xj_engine_earliest_landing(boundary, out_chain_micros)` for NOW, BEAT, BAR (barBeats of the current main program), SEGMENT, MAIN (next NextMain) and MACRO with exact integer micros. Tests at 30, 120 and 180 bpm and at segment edges.

tasks.title: Implement the cue queue, cut-at-boundary rewrite, cancel and the landing acknowledgement
tasks.summary: Add the cue struct (type, boundary, payload; `xj_cue` is its ABI mirror), a pending-cue queue in CraftWork, public documented `XJ::Engine::cue()`, `cancelCue()` and `earliestLanding()` methods (Q8: the C++ API remains first-class, so Unreal reaches cues without the ABI), `cue()` landing the cue at `earliest_landing(boundary)`, the first boundary of that kind at or beyond the commit horizon (a BAR cue whose next downbeat is inside the horizon lands on the following bar and the UI says 'lands in 2 bars'), returning a refusal status only for XJ_BOUNDARY_NOW (or an absolute landing, if one is ever added) that falls inside the horizon, and `cancel_cue()`. Generalize doFabricationRewrite and doCutoffLastSegment to cut the current segment at the chosen boundary rather than at `barBeats × cutoffMinimumBars` after the deadline (one exact beats-to-micros formula replaces the three; the legacy cut point stays available as an internal landing rule for the override wrappers), and record a landing acknowledgement (cue id, landing chain micros) as a message. Two foundation cues at the same boundary apply in arrival order, second wins, with a collision message (Q13).

tasks.title: Re-implement doOverrideMacro and doOverrideMemes as Macro and Memes cues, quirks kept
tasks.summary: The existing override functions become thin wrappers that enqueue a Macro or Memes cue with an internal, non-ABI landing rule `legacy_cutoff` (the next multiple of barBeats × cutoffMinimumBars after at + deadlineMicros, engine-api-lifecycle §8) that no `xj_boundary` value expresses, so `xj_engine_override_*` and the C++ overrides keep 1.9.6 timing exactly while new hosts use the cue boundaries, preserving in addition the two quirks (an overridden macro starts at its second binding offset; a meme override empties the retrospective) so EngineTest, the Unreal plugin and the Java-era control modes behave exactly as before. Document both quirks in the cue spec as inherited behavior.

tasks.title: Implement the Advance and Hold cues with a NextMain landing path
tasks.summary: The existing rewrite path always forces the new segment to NextMacro (CraftWork.cpp:321), so Advance ('leave the current section') needs a new path that produces a NextMain segment at the boundary, and Hold keeps the next segment at the same sequence binding offset instead of advancing. Implement both through the cue queue with tests on the segment type and binding offsets.

tasks.title: Implement the Chord cue with first-chord forcing and a chord-level transposition primitive
tasks.summary: A Chord cue cuts at the boundary and crafts the next segment with its first chord forced; main-program selection prefers a sequence whose first chord matches, else transposes. The optional key (04 §6, 08 §Cues: 'chord name, optional key') is the target key when present: main-program selection prefers a sequence in that key whose first chord matches, else the chosen sequence is transposed into it, and it is written as the next segment's `Segment.key`; when the key is null only the first chord is forced and the segment key is left to the chosen main program as today. The engine has no `Chord::transpose`: add one (shift root and slash pitch class with Step::step, keep the description verbatim, inherit the source accidental), parse incoming names with `Chord::of` and store canonical names, and use the explicit no-chord representation the segment serializer task owns (an explicit null, since `NC` has no stable spelling). Tests cover slash chords and enharmonic equality via `Chord::operator==`.

tasks.title: Implement the Intensity cue with a ramp and Layer Mute as a deterministic per-type flag
tasks.summary: Intensity is applied in dub with a ramp in beats (new) and interacts with the restored crescendo. Layer Mute cannot be 'set choiceMuteProbability to 1' as written: the roll is per segment and never inherited, so it would flicker, and it used to throw at 1.0. Implement a per-type mute flag consulted where getChoiceMuteProbability is read, and flip `SegmentChoice::mute` on already-crafted, not-yet-dubbed segments so the mute and un-mute land at the next segment without a re-craft.

tasks.title: Write the cue test family: boundary exactness, NOW-only refusal, cancel and collisions
tasks.summary: For each of the seven cue types and each boundary, assert the landing chain micros equal `earliest_landing(boundary)` and never fall inside the commit horizon (a BEAT or BAR cue whose next boundary is inside the horizon lands on the following one and is never refused), that only a NOW cue inside the horizon is refused with a status, that a Chord cue with a key sets the next segment's key and one without leaves the main program's, that cancel removes a pending cue, that two foundation cues at one boundary apply in arrival order, and that ambient tempos (30 bpm, 512 s sequences) still land on BAR and BEAT boundaries. Uses the sub-seed so expected stores are exact.

tasks.title: Implement the External tempo policy with boundary-only tests and the 20 to 999 bpm rule
tasks.summary: Add the Content|External policy and a pending external tempo as public documented `XJ::Engine::setTempoPolicy()` and `setExternalTempo()` methods (Q8). In External mode MacroMainCraft writes the external tempo to the segment; CraftWork.cpp:300 (rewrite) must read `lastSegment->tempo` instead of `currentMainProgram->tempo` so it agrees with doCutoffLastSegment at :336 (edited after the horizon task has unified the three beats-to-micros formulas, so the two tasks touch those lines in order); and the segment tempo must be written before the Fabricator's first beats-to-micros call because getMicrosPerBeat caches the first tempo it sees. Main programs are still chosen by memes; their nominal tempo becomes advisory. Tests assert that a tempo change affects only segments crafted after it, that scheduled audio micros are unchanged, that the engine either runs across Link's 20 to 999 bpm range or applies a documented ×2/÷2 lock (TEST-PLAN TEMPO-4), and that Link's integer micros-per-beat quantization (124 bpm is 483,871 µs) is tolerated by comparing beats, not micros. The pending external tempo and the boundary at which it lands are recorded as a SegmentMessage so hosts read them through `xj_engine_get_messages_json`; no further ABI function is introduced for tempo state.

tasks.title: Define the foundation record JSON, its schema, and the C++ serializer and parser
tasks.summary: Implement the register's record (segment{id, segmentType, beginBeat, beginChainMicros, totalBeats, barBeats, key, tempo, intensity, delta}, chords, voicings, memes, foundationChoice) plus what the code needs: `barBeats` is new (it lives only in ProgramConfig today), `durationMicros` is required by five later-stage call sites, voicings allow several per chord per instrument type, `foundationChoice` carries an opaque main-sequence identity because isMediumTransitionSegment compares sequence ids, chord names are canonical `Chord::of(...).getName()` with the explicit null for no-chord the segment serializers define, and `SegmentChordVoicing.type` is spelled as its string. Publish a JSON Schema; the engine side omits the session envelope.

tasks.title: Implement the Internal/External foundation source setting and conduct-mode publication
tasks.summary: Add the Internal|External foundation-source setting on the C++ engine (the register names only the ABI enum `xj_foundation_source`; the ABI function `xj_engine_set_foundation_source` belongs to the foundation ABI task) and a conduct flag (`WorkSettings::conductEnabled`; the ABI create field `conduct_enabled` and its `runtime` introspection keys belong to the foundation ABI task); after each segment is crafted in Internal mode, make its foundation available through a C++ `Engine::getFoundationJson(segmentId)` in the record format (the ABI wrapper `xj_engine_get_foundation_json` and its C test belong to the foundation ABI task, as `xj_engine_set_foundation_source` already does), with `barBeats` filled from the main program's config. Read-only; the conductor's own craft is unchanged.

tasks.title: Implement ExternalFoundationCraft running in place of MacroMainCraft on pushed records
tasks.summary: Consume records pushed through the foundation queue, write Segment (type, key, tempo, total, durationMicros recomputed exactly as segmentLengthMicros does, delta, intensity) via updateSegment after Planned to Crafting, chords, voicings (several per chord per type allowed) and memes. Pass the record's type as `overrideSegmentType` to the Fabricator because `getType()` otherwise consults content bindings the follower may not have, and write placeholder macro/main SegmentChoices with stable opaque program identities so SegmentRetrospective does not throw 'sees no main choice' on the second segment. Store semantics are insert_or_assign so a re-pushed record for the same segment replaces.

tasks.title: Reject foundation cues in follow mode with a status; intensity and layer cues stay local
tasks.summary: When the foundation source is External, `cue()` refuses Macro, Memes, Chord, Advance and Hold with a distinct follow-mode status so the station can forward them as cue requests; Intensity and Layer Mute are accepted and applied locally because intensity and layering are per-station decisions. Tests cover every cue type in both sources and the switch between them at a segment boundary.

tasks.title: Answer the direct main-program reads from the foundation record in follow mode
tasks.summary: The verified list of content reads that bypass segment entities: `barBeats` at Craft.cpp:85 and TransitionCraft.cpp:85, current and previous main-sequence identity at TransitionCraft.cpp:45-51, and the rewrite's `barBeats × cutoffMinimumBars` plus tempo in CraftWork.cpp:283-300. In follow mode the Fabricator answers the first two from the current and previous records, and the rewrite takes bar length from the record and cutoffMinimumBars from the follower's template. The fourth reader is 2.0's own: `earliest_landing(BAR)` and the cue cut take `barBeats` from the current main program, and in External mode there is none, so both read `segment.barBeats` from the current record. Tests per site, including a BAR cue on a follower.

tasks.title: Exclude Beat and Detail programs whose barBeats differ from the segment's (Q14)
tasks.summary: In `chooseFreshProgram` (Craft.cpp:159-165) exclude any Beat or Detail program whose `ProgramConfig.barBeats` differs from the segment's bar length (these are the two callers of chooseFreshProgram; Transition and Background choose instruments only and have no barBeats, so Q14's 'transition or background program' wording is corrected by p0-docs-amend-proposal-after-spikes; Loop-mode audio `loopBeats` is not checked against the bar here), in follow mode and as a free improvement in internal mode, writing a SegmentMessage ('excluded: 3-beat program against a 4-beat segment'). A follower with no matching material plays nothing for that layer rather than something that drifts.

tasks.title: Implement hold when the timeline runs dry, fallback to Internal, and rejoin at NextMacro
tasks.summary: When no record exists for the next segment, fabricate Continue segments repeating the last foundation with a warning SegmentMessage, for up to followHoldMaxBars; then switch the source to Internal at the boundary and continue alone. Rejoin equals join: a NextMacro segment aligned to the conductor's next boundary. Tests starve the follower, assert the hold count, the fallback and a clean rejoin with no gap.

tasks.title: Write the two-engines-one-process follow-mode test: identical foundations per span
tasks.summary: Construct a conducting and a following engine in one process over the richer fixture, feed each conductor record to the follower, and assert for every segment span that key, tempo, chords, voicings and memes are equal (compare beats and canonical names, not micros or spellings) and that the follower's beat and detail choices are valid against them. Runs on all three CI platforms; this is the Phase 1 exit demonstration.

tasks.title: Implement Engine::preview over a scratch store copy; test preview equals the real result
tasks.summary: A public, documented `XJ::Engine::preview(const Cue&)` C++ method (the ABI wrapper `xj_engine_preview_cue_json` and its C test are the ABI task's). Copy the store tail (nine value-semantic maps), apply the cue, craft the next segment into the copy with the segment's sub-seed, serialize macro and main names, key, chords, memes, intensity and the instruments that would play, then discard the copy; no raw pointer escapes. Test that the preview equals the store after actually sending the cue, for every cue type.

tasks.title: Record candidates, weights and exclusions behind a diagnostics flag at both gates
tasks.summary: Two exclusion gates exist: the silent `iso.isAllowed` at bag time and the put-time MemeStack check that already writes an Error message. Zero cost when off; snapshot JSON includes them. The flag itself is exposed to hosts by the ABI task `p1-abi-diagnostics-flag` (create setting plus `xj_engine_set_diagnostics`).

tasks.summary: Add `xj_cue` (type, boundary, payload; the Chord payload carries the chord name and the optional key with an explicit null), the `xj_boundary` and `xj_cue_type` enums, `xj_engine_cue`, `xj_engine_cancel_cue`, `xj_engine_earliest_landing(boundary, out_chain_micros)`, `xj_tempo_policy` with `xj_engine_set_tempo_policy` and `xj_engine_set_external_tempo`, and `xj_engine_set_seed` / `xj_engine_get_seed` (wrapping `Engine::setSeed`/`getSeed` from p1-det-rng-primitives, since 1.9.6 has no seed setter: the seed must be set before `xj_engine_start`; the drawn seed is reported when unset). Extend the C11 test program for each function.

tasks.summary: Each function wraps a public documented `XJ::Engine` method (`setFoundationSource`, `pushFoundationJson`, `getFoundationJson`) so Unreal reaches follow mode through the C++ API (Q8). Add the `xj_foundation_source` enum {Internal, External}, `xj_engine_set_foundation_source`, `xj_engine_push_foundation_json` (queued records, validated against the schema, with a status for a record that arrives too late to craft against, the engine-side rule for which, hold that one segment and warn, is the hold/rejoin task's) and `xj_engine_get_foundation_json` (the record for a crafted segment, engine side without the session envelope). The follow-mode refusal of `xj_engine_cue` (Macro, Memes, Chord, Advance, Hold while the source is External) gets its own `xj_status` code here, distinct from the NOW-inside-horizon code. C tests push a conductor's records into a second handle and read them back, and assert the follow-mode code on a Macro cue sent to the follower. With this group and the preview wrapper the surface listed in the register is complete; the 1.0.0 freeze is the baseline the stability check captures at the tag.

tasks.title: Add xj_engine_reload_content so content edits take effect at the next segment boundary
tasks.summary: 05-workstation assumes that 'edits to content take effect at the next segment boundary, which is already how the engine reloads'; no such path exists (projectContent is loaded once in the constructor and ActiveAudio holds raw pointers into it). Add `xj_engine_reload_content(json, len)` (part of ABI 1.0.0 since it blocks the 2.0.0 tag; one of the register's new names, listed in the rationale) that parses a replacement payload off the hot path, swaps it in between cycles at the next segment boundary, keeps the previous store alive until no scheduled audio references it, and rejects payloads that drop the running template. Consumed by the Java-handoff reload in Phase 3 and by the Rust editors in Phase 6. Extend the C11 test program: reload a payload mid-chain and assert the swap lands at the boundary and the running template cannot be dropped.

tasks.title: Add xj_engine_set_horizons: craft-ahead, dub-ahead, deadline and a commit-horizon override
tasks.summary: Settings are copied into WorkManager at start and there is no runtime setter, yet a follower's craft horizon derives from the conductor's `welcome` and the settings screen offers horizons while the music plays. Add `xj_engine_set_horizons(craft_ahead_micros, dub_ahead_micros, deadline_micros, commit_horizon_beats)` (part of ABI 1.0.0, a new name beside `xj_engine_reload_content`) that validates the values, applies them at the next segment boundary without touching already-dubbed audio, and reports the boundary as a message. `commit_horizon_beats` is an optional host override of the template's `commitHorizonBeats` (a value of 0 or less keeps the template key; a positive host value wins), because 05 and 08 define the horizon as 'default one beat in Play mode' while the template default reproduces the 1.9.x game horizon, so a V1 project opened in Play mode must get the Play-mode horizon from the host, not from its template. A C test changes horizons mid-chain and asserts no segment is re-timed and no audio inside the old dub window is revoked, and a second C test sets a one-beat override on a template without the key and asserts `xj_engine_earliest_landing(BEAT)` moves accordingly at the next segment boundary.

tasks.title: Expose the choice-diagnostics flag through the ABI create settings and a C test
tasks.summary: 04-engine §8 puts choice diagnostics behind a flag so game integrations pay nothing, and the why panel wants it on in Play mode, but no ABI function or create-time setting sets it. Add `diagnostics_enabled` to the create settings struct and `xj_engine_set_diagnostics(bool)` over a public `XJ::Engine::setDiagnostics(bool)` applied at the next segment boundary (both listed among the register's new names beside `xj_engine_reload_content` and `xj_engine_set_horizons`), default off, and extend the C11 test program to turn it on and read an `xj.choice.*` SegmentMeta back through `xj_engine_get_segments_json`, and to assert no such meta appears when it is off.

Extend engine/test/c/xj_c_test.c: preview every cue type, then send the cue and assert the preview equals `xj_engine_get_segments_json` of the crafted segment; assert the buffer is replaced, not leaked, across two consecutive previews. Done when the preview group has its C test like every other register group and the Doxygen freeze and ABI baseline include it.

tasks.title: Parse the three new InstrumentConfig keys and tolerate contentHash and origin fields
tasks.summary: Add the three InstrumentConfig keys with defaults that reproduce today's behavior, emit them in toString(), and make the content loader tolerate `contentHash` on InstrumentAudio and `originPack`/`originVersion` on every entity (unknown keys are already ignored on read; this records them). Document the HOCON-subset typing rule for the new float.

tasks.title: Rank shifted samples under allowPitchShift and request stretch_ratio for Loop audio
tasks.summary: Pitch shift: the only place the engine knows it has no exact-tone audio is `selectNewMultiphonicInstrumentAudio` (Craft.cpp:974-1010), which warns and drops the pick; monophonic non-Drum selection (Craft.cpp:953-972) scores by raw event tones and never fails, playing the lowest-UUID audio when nothing matches, so the monophonic path needs its own rule: when allowPitchShift is set, rank candidates by semitone distance from the picked voicing note within pitchShiftRange, exact tone first, and request the shift on the pick; without the flag the 1.9.6 scoring is unchanged. When allowPitchShift is set, rank exact-tone candidates first and others by semitone distance within pitchShiftRange (decide whether octave-equivalent samples count as exact, since Note::operator== compares octave), record the shift on the pick and set `pitch_shift_semitones` on the schedule event. Stretch: `DetailCraft::craftLoopParts` never reads `audio->tempo` (the concrete G7 gap); when the instrument allows stretch and is in Loop mode set `stretch_ratio = segmentTempo / audio.tempo` on the pick and event; Background picks have no beat length so stretch does not apply, and the field is scoped to Loop mode because elsewhere `tempo` is the creation default. Deterministic through the chain Rng.

tasks.title: Prove engine 2.0 reads every 1.9.x project unchanged with a compatibility fixture suite
tasks.summary: Load the four checked-in demo build payloads, the engine test project and the richer fixture through both the path and in-memory loaders; assert identical choices with and without the new fields present, that unknown keys are ignored, that voice and track names load, that `"tempo": 120` reads as 120, and that non-UUID content ids map to stable 16-byte ids with a warning. This is the acceptance test for 04-engine §12's promise.

tasks.summary: Typed `Cue`, `Boundary` and payload enums; `cue()`, `cancel_cue()`, `earliest_landing()`, the three existing overrides, `set_tempo_policy`/`set_external_tempo`, `set_seed`/`seed`, and `preview()` returning a typed struct. tasks.title: Implement the canonical V1 writer and the V2 sidecar for additive fields
tasks.summary: Write the five file kinds with Jackson's getter order, per-type `compareTo` sorting, `NON_NULL`/`NON_EMPTY` inclusion, `"demo": false` on every file, floats with a fractional part (the engine ignores `120`), the `toAlphanumericHyphenated` slug rule and deletion of stale files in libraries/ and templates/. tasks.title: Run a Java-Rust-Java round-trip of every demo project on each PR until Java is archived
tasks.summary: CI job: Java writer output (fixture) read by xj-content, written back, read by the Java `ProjectManagerImpl` in a small JVM harness, compared as parsed trees (byte identity is not a goal because pretty-printer styles differ). Covers all four demos and the legacy fixture; this is the R14 mitigation and it runs from Phase 2 to the Phase 6 archive.

tasks.title: Synthesize the merged engine payload in memory and map waveform keys to audio paths
tasks.summary: The engine reads only the `.xj` and `build/**/*.json`; xj-content must synthesize the merged HubContent-shaped payload and hand it to `xj_engine_load_project` (the new `Engine::loadProjectContent(json, audioRoot)`) with an audio root, mapping `waveformKey` (original name in libraries/, `<audioId>.ext` after Build, `<blake3>.ext` in packs) to a file. Resolve the template by name, then shipKey, then id before reaching the engine.

tasks.title: Implement Build for engine: build/<audioId>.wav at 48 kHz 16-bit stereo plus merged JSON
tasks.summary: Reproduce the Java Build: every entity of every template, orphans removed, each audio decoded and resampled to 48 kHz 16-bit stereo WAV named `<InstrumentAudio.id>.wav` (hound Int16, PCMWAVEFORMAT header), `waveformKey` rewritten, `build/<slug>.json` written, skip-if-matching by reading the destination header. Compare against a Java Build of Hero's Journey in CI as format-compatible, not byte-identical (rubato replaces libswresample): identical file names, an equivalent fmt chunk (PCM, 48000 Hz, 16-bit, 2 channels; the Java Build writes through javacv's FFmpegFrameRecorder, whose wav muxer adds a LIST/INFO chunk, so header bytes are not compared) with the Unreal importer accepting both, semantically equal `build/<slug>.json`, and audio within a stated tolerance, so the Unreal plugin keeps working on day one.

tasks.title: Port the chord and note grammar to Rust, verified against the engine's YAML fixture
tasks.summary: A Rust `Chord::of`/`Note::of` with the 41 canonical forms and synonyms (case-sensitive M-family), slash-root rules, the sharp/flat tie rule, scientific-pitch octaves (C4 = MIDI 60), verified against engine/test/_data/music_chord_test.yaml and the oracle outputs. Mirrors the spec's explicit null for no-chord and the four-line `Chord::transpose` recipe (shift root and slash pitch class, keep the description, inherit the accidental), cross-checked against the engine once the Chord cue and serializers land, by the chord-picker task that consumes both; used by lint, the chord picker and foundation parsing; equality is enharmonic, never string compare.

tasks.title: Port the ConfigParser dialect to Rust with the canonical sorted formatter
tasks.summary: A Rust parser and formatter for the engine's HOCON subset: `key = value` lines, values typed by literal shape (`1` int, `1.0` float, quoted strings, bare lists and the structured memeTaxonomy list-of-objects), no comments, substitutions, path keys or nested objects, and the sorted canonical output the C++ `toString()` emits. Verified against every case in engine/test/util/ConfigParserTest.cpp and the four demo templates' config strings round-tripped through the C++ formatter in CI, with the 2.0 keys (commitHorizonBeats, followHoldMaxBars, mixerFiltersEnabled, allowPitchShift, pitchShiftRange, allowStretch) in the canonical key set, taken from the register by name so the port does not wait for the C++ parsers; the lint task, which runs after both, asserts the two formatters agree on them. Consumed by lint, show composition and the Phase 6 config editors.

tasks.title: Decode with symphonia 0.6 using explicit features and the demo chunk-layout fixtures
tasks.summary: Enable `wav`, `pcm`, `flac`, `ogg`, `vorbis` plus `mp3`, `aac`, `isomp4`, `aiff` explicitly (defaults exclude MP3, AAC, MP4, AIFF, ALAC); state that HE-AAC, Opus and WavPack are unsupported. Decode 24-bit packed PCM and 32-bit float, trust the `data` chunk size, and add fixtures for the layouts found in the demos: JUNK-first (2,256 files), Broadcast Wave with bext/minf/elm1 and a 1,024-byte data offset, cue/LIST/smpl chunks, odd data sizes, trailing chunks.

tasks.title: Resample with rubato 5 without changing channel count and benchmark 88.2 to 48 kHz
tasks.summary: Async sinc resampling via `process_into_buffer` only (allocation-free), mono stays mono (the Java cache up-mixed mono at the wrong rate to stereo), pinned to rubato 5 and audioadapter 5. Benchmark the realistic case: 815 of 3,000 demo files are 88.2 kHz, so Deep House's 4.5 GB at 88.2 to 48 is the cache-fill benchmark, not 44.1 to 48.

tasks.title: Hash sources with BLAKE3 and store exact device-rate entries in a budgeted disk tier
tasks.summary: ContentHash with buffered reads (no mmap of user files) and a persistent (len, mtime) hash index; CacheKey and a total VariantSpec::from_event with no instrumentId (the Java key had no content identity, so replaced samples were invisible); the .xjpcm format storing i24 or i16 with 6 dB headroom and exact ties-even quantization so cold and warm caches give bit-identical buffers; the passthrough rule for device-rate PCM; a disk tier with cross-process mtime LRU eviction and an ENOSPC fallback, sized against 27.7 GB of decoded demos; one blocking materialize call.

tasks.title: Build the memory tier, preload worker pool and AudioCache API over the disk tier
tasks.summary: A memory tier with a pinned working set and budget, a deadline-ordered decode worker pool that preloads audio for picks inside the craft-ahead window (as Java's doAudioCacheMaintenance did) and hands immutable Arc<SampleBuffer>s to the DSP by reference, revalidation that detects replaced source files during a session, and the AudioCache API (try_get with queue-on-miss, warm with variants, retarget after a device rate change, fingerprint for replay). The UI reads stats from the station snapshot, never through a shared mutex.

tasks.title: Render stretched and shifted variants ahead of time with the Q2 library (Signalsmith)
tasks.summary: Vendor Signalsmith Stretch 1.3.2 and Signalsmith Linear from upstream via `cc` (the crates.io wrapper pins a June 2025 commit; `process()` can allocate, which confirms it must never run on the audio thread) behind one `Stretcher` trait, using upstream's seeded constructor and whole-buffer `exact()` call for reproducible, latency-compensated offline renders. If the Q2 blind session chooses Bungee (MPL-2.0, grain API, CMake build, no maintained Rust binding), this task is re-specified before it starts. Render a variant for each (hash, ratio, semitones) the engine requests via `pitch_shift_semitones`/`stretch_ratio`, store it in the cache, and expose the lookups the station uses when converting schedule events. Loop stretch is scoped to Loop-mode instruments.

tasks.title: Implement the four time bases and the continuously re-estimated affine maps
tasks.summary: Chain micros as an affine function of device frames, re-estimated continuously; a per-stream `StreamInstant` to host-microsecond regression (512 points like HostTimeFilter) with a direct-conversion fast path on macOS and WASAPI after a startup sanity check; beat time from the BeatClock. Segment chain begins derive from `time_at_beat(beginBeat)` rather than summed durations so Link's integer micros-per-beat and the engine's rounding cannot drift apart over a show. Nothing outside xj-transport converts. The structural facts (per-stream StreamInstant regression; direct conversion only on macOS and WASAPI) come from source reading; the per-device output-latency trim values arrive from the Phase 0 AUDIOENGINE-1 measurement as settings consumed by the `link` implementation, so this task does not wait on that hardware measurement.

tasks.title: Define the BeatClock trait and the internal clock implementation
tasks.summary: Trait methods per the gap map's mapping table: now_micros, beat_at(t, quantum), phase_at, time_at_beat, next_downbeat_after, tempo_bpm, set_tempo, anchor_beat, is_playing, peers, ClockEvent::Tempo/Peers/Transport/Resync drained from events() once per control tick (no on_* callbacks into station code), refresh and host_clock from BeatTimeline, as_any/as_any_mut, stream_to_host, output_latency, dac_time_of_buffer_start. The internal implementation runs a station alone with quantum equal to the current barBeats.

tasks.title: Fork the Link binding under the workspace, pin Link 4.1.1 and harden it for the callback
tasks.summary: rusty_link 0.4.9 on crates.io vendors Link 4.0.0b3 (its `abl_link_create` returns a LinkAudio instance), is GPL-2.0-or-later, and is a one-person project last touched 2026-01. Fork it under the XJ workspace as recorded in Phase 0, pin Ableton/link 4.1.1 (CMake 3.18, C++17), keep LinkAudio disabled, fix HostTimeFilter::reset allocation and the two asserts that would panic in the callback, and confirm by packet capture that a LinkAudio-disabled instance interoperates with Link 3 peers (MPC firmware). Ableton's grant can cover the vendored Link and abl_link; the rusty_link-derived Rust files are isolated in src/derived/ and need their author's relicense or the Phase 3 rewrite.

tasks.title: Implement the link BeatClock behind a feature flag with the one-writer and TEST-PLAN rules
tasks.summary: Over the binding fork pinned to Link 4.1.1: SessionState allocated once outside the callback and moved in; all commits from exactly one side (audio thread via a lock-free command queue, as LinkHut does); construct with the current bpm and never push a template tempo when peers > 0 (TEMPO-2/3/5); keep the last tempo on disable; magnitudes use the quantum pinned at construction and phase uses the current barBeats, so a barBeats change never moves the grid; start/stop sync off by default; no re-anchoring (request_beat_at_time is never called, Q3 Decision 4). Compiled only with `--features link`, which is enabled in official builds only once the license is on file. The per-host output-latency offsets and the DAC-time rule come from the Phase 0 AUDIOENGINE-1 measurement, and the tempo range policy (20 to 999 bpm, or the documented ×2/÷2 lock) is applied by the station's tempo wiring, which waits for the engine's External tempo tests; the clock itself does not.

tasks.title: Convert schedule events to DSP commands at absolute device frames and count late commands
tasks.summary: Each Create/Update/Delete becomes StartVoice/UpdateVoice/StopVoice stamped with an absolute device frame from the affine map, placing the file's onset (the engine pre-shifts by transientSeconds) on the beat with the buffer handle the station supplies (plain decoded audio first; pre-rendered variants once the station resolves them). Commands whose frame is already past are applied at the next buffer and counted; the counter is the first diagnostic to look at when something feels late. Tests simulate drift and tempo change and assert zero late commands and beat-accurate frames.
proposal_refs: 03-architecture.md Data flow in one engine cycle

tasks.title: Implement the SPSC command ring and the full DSP command set with frame stamping
tasks.summary: rtrb (>= 0.4.0) single-producer single-consumer ring carrying the register's command set (StartVoice, UpdateVoice, StopVoice, TriggerOneShot, SetBusGain/Mute/Solo, SetFxParam, SetMasterParams, CaptureStart/Stop), each with an absolute device frame; commands in the past apply at the next buffer boundary and increment a counter the meter ring reports. Written down as the second contract.

tasks.title: Implement the fixed voice pool: gain spans, quarter-sine release, opt-in attack, channels
tasks.summary: 256 pre-allocated voices playing immutable buffers by reference; gain glides from gain_from to gain_to over an explicit frame span (V1 ramped per 1 s chunk, which the spec records as the behavior being replaced); release is the Java quarter-sine `sin(pi/2 * i/N)` fade of the still-playing source, default 5 ms; an attack ramp exists as an opt-in voice parameter that defaults to 0 frames (05 §Voices defines the envelope as the gain span plus release and V1 had no attack; 2,905 of 3,000 demo audios have transientSeconds 0, so a default attack would soften every drum hit), used only as click protection when a voice is stopped before it started; mono sources duplicate to both channels and stereo-to-mono sums per a stated rule. A voice past its stop enters release and is reclaimed when silent.

tasks.title: Allocate ten typed buses plus master with gain, mute, solo ramps and meters
tasks.summary: Buses are allocated up front for the ten `Instrument::Type` strings (not ordinals, which differ between C++ and Java) plus a master; each has gain from dubMasterVolume, mute and solo with ramp frames, and per-bus peak, RMS and momentary-loudness meters written to a ring buffer the UI reads at frame rate. `SetBusGain`, `SetBusMute` and `SetBusSolo` carry bus, value and ramp_frames per the command set.

tasks.title: Port the logarithmic DRC and look-ahead compressor; record the default-is-unity decision
tasks.summary: Port MathUtil.logarithmicCompression and the compressor (ratio re-targeted every dspBufferSize frames from a look-ahead peak scan, second-order smoothed per frame) with SetMasterParams populated from TemplateConfig only. Record that under template defaults (ratioMax 1.0 after the log stage) the compressor is a unity stage, define V2 look-ahead semantics with a true ring buffer (50 ms offline; 1 ms live with a window that scans every frame, inside the 10 ms gesture budget) since bit-identity with the chunked Java version is impossible, and record where the demos' non-default mixerCompressToAmplitude makes live and offline differ, and decide whether to keep the inert defaults.

tasks.title: Add master high-pass and low-pass filters and an in-house true-peak safety limiter
tasks.summary: Filters: no high-pass or low-pass DSP exists in the Java mixer (`mixerHighpassThresholdHz` and `mixerLowpassThresholdHz` were parsed and never read), and both keys are present in every template (TemplateConfig::DEFAULT sets 30 Hz and 15 kHz), so implement second-order Butterworth filters from those keys and enable them only when the station passes `filters_enabled` in SetMasterParams (the station reads the new `mixerFiltersEnabled` key from the template config JSON; the DSP never reads the engine), and state in the release notes that enabling them changes the sound of existing templates. Limiter: no mature true-peak limiter crate exists; implement a look-ahead limiter with 4x oversampled peak detection at the master output, ceiling -1.0 dBTP, verified with `ebur128` (Mode::TRUE_PEAK) over the golden renders and an hour of random content. This replaces the Java path where 16-bit conversion wrapped above full scale.

tasks.title: Prove the full audio graph never allocates, locks or blocks, and promote the callback
tasks.summary: A test harness with a counting global allocator and a lock detector runs the full graph, including the capture sink's audio-thread half (CaptureStart/CaptureStop and the hand-off to the writer thread), for minutes of simulated callbacks and fails on any allocation or lock; add xrun and late-command counters; use cpal's `realtime` feature for thread promotion (Linux needs CAP_SYS_NICE, rtprio or `realtime-dbus`). Rules enforced by construction per 03-architecture.

tasks.title: Implement the per-bus insert effects: SVF, tempo-synced delay, short reverb, saturator
tasks.summary: Four insert slots per bus addressed by SetFxParam with ramped parameters: SVF (cutoff, resonance, mode), delay synced to a tempo the station sends through SetFxParam (time in beats, feedback, mix; xj-dsp does not depend on xj-transport), a short algorithmic reverb (size, mix), and a saturator (drive, mix). Allocation-free, bypass at unity when untouched, and never visible to the engine.

tasks.title: Implement the cpal device sink on CoreAudio, WASAPI, PipeWire, JACK and ALSA; recover loss
tasks.summary: cpal 0.18.2: streams must be `play()`ed, default config prefers 48 kHz, DeviceChanged notification was reverted so device loss is detected from the stream error callback and followed by rescan and reopen with transport re-estimation; ALSA `default` fails with DeviceBusy under PipeWire, so on Linux the sink enumerates hosts and the station settings expose a host choice (PipeWire, the default and the supported tier; JACK through cpal's `jack` feature, built into official Linux binaries; ALSA direct) with the chosen host's devices listed, per the Q10 record's Linux tiers (PipeWire supported, JACK and ALSA best-effort) so a venue running JACK or bare ALSA has a stated path; the `asio` feature compiles only behind the flag and downloads Steinberg's SDK at build time, so official builds leave it off until countersignature. Buffer size configurable, default 256 frames.

tasks.title: Implement the segmented WAV capture sink and the null sink with an offline render driver
tasks.summary: WAV: a writer thread fed from the audio thread writes master and optionally per-bus WAVs with hound 3.5.1 (Int24 or Float32, which switches the header to WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE); hound's data length is u32 with no RF64, so 3.1 h of f32 overflows silently: segment files at a size threshold snapped to segment, main or macro boundaries, reinstating the V1 nexus OutputFileMode behavior, with CaptureStart/CaptureStop commands and a manifest of segments per capture. Null: a sink that consumes buffers against a synthetic clock so the same graph renders N minutes as fast as the CPU allows, advancing chain time deterministically for Ship-mode bounce, lint renders and CI.

tasks.title: Add golden render tests from the Java DemoIT fixtures and audio-statistics assertions
tasks.summary: Reuse DemoIT's 16-step 121 bpm drum pattern and source WAVs as a cross-implementation fixture compared with a tolerance (the resampler differs, so byte identity is not a goal), and add statistics helpers (silence detection, clipping, integrated loudness via ebur128, true peak) used by CI render jobs and the lint.

tasks.title: Implement MIDI input over midir with rescan, the tiered match key and in/out pairing
tasks.summary: midir has no hot-plug callback on any backend: rescan `ports()` on a 1 to 2 s timer, detect loss by set difference, recreate `MidiInput` on macOS. Identity is a tiered key: port-name glob (tolerating ALSA's 31-char truncation and Windows' 'MIDIIN2 (...)'), Universal Device Inquiry reply, optional best-effort USB VID:PID; never persist `id()`. Pair input and output by name stem confirmed by the inquiry round trip; parse `9n` velocity 0 as release; re-stamp every event with the station's monotonic clock.

tasks.title: Implement OSC over UDP, keyboard and gamepad inputs
tasks.summary: rosc is a codec only: add the UDP transport with bundles and timetags, plus sending for integrations such as lighting desks. gilrs for gamepads (polling, hot-plug supported) and a raw-mode keyboard reader for the CLI so the whole surface can be driven without a controller.

tasks.title: Define the mapping TOML schema (notes, CCs, program changes, NRPN) with CLI learn mode
tasks.summary: `[profile]` with the tiered match and an instance slot (two Launchpads look identical), `[[map]]` entries binding an input (MIDI note, CC, program change or NRPN by number, OSC address, key or gamepad control) to a cue, gesture, move or session action with an optional `led` block, `[moves.<name>].steps`, and a `capabilities` block (colors, blink, max_batch). Names resolve against the loaded show and unresolved ones are flagged. Learn mode prints what you touched and writes the profile. A pack may ship profiles and moves in an optional `mapping/` folder so a performer's vocabulary travels with the content.

tasks.title: Route mapped inputs: cues to the engine at a boundary, gestures to the DSP quantized
tasks.summary: Cues (Macro, Memes, Intensity, Chord, Advance, Hold, LayerMute) go to the station scheduler with their boundary and carry the preview and landing-time metadata the UI shows; gestures become DSP commands stamped with the device frame of the next buffer or quantized to none, beat, half-beat or bar through the transport, so they are audible within one buffer and the engine never learns of them. A layer mute sends both the gesture and the cue. Every input is re-stamped with the station's monotonic clock on receipt, since midir timestamps are per-backend. A `[[map]]` entry or move step that omits `boundary` takes 08's default per cue type (Macro, Memes, Advance, Hold and Layer Mute: Segment; Intensity: Beat; Chord: Bar); the surface's cue-boundary selector overrides that default for foundation cues sent from the screen (05 §Cue boundary).
proposal_refs: 03-architecture.md Data flow in one engine cycle

tasks.title: Implement the gestures: one-shot, bus mute, solo and gain, FX params, stutter and fill
tasks.summary: OneShot plays an InstrumentAudio of the running template on its bus (its decoded buffer comes as an Arc from the content cache's preload path) (TriggerOneShot, quantize none/beat/half-beat); BusMute/BusSolo (none/beat/bar) and ramped BusGain; FxParam for filter cutoff and resonance, delay time and feedback, reverb mix and saturation with curves; Stutter retriggers the current voices on a bus at a beat division for as long as held; Fill plays a designated fill sample on the Drum bus at the next bar while muting the Drum voices under it. Each gesture is logged with its frame for replay.

tasks.title: Implement moves: composed cues and gestures with relative timing, replayable, previewable
tasks.summary: Steps with `at = "beat" | "bar" | "segment" | "bar+4"` scheduled against the transport; the canonical drop (mute all but Drum at the beat, intensity 0.2 with a 16-beat ramp at the bar, Advance at the segment, unmute at bar+4). Preview renders the engine's cue previews plus a text description of the gesture steps; execution is logged for replay. Moves are saved in the mapping profile and are shareable as part of a pack.

tasks.title: Implement four-state LED feedback and ship the Launchpad Mini MK3 and MPD218 profiles
tasks.summary: Off, available, armed and active from the same mapping, with armed and active driven by the pending-cue scheduler state the routing task produces and by the engine snapshot. Launchpad: palette index on channel 1 static, channel 2 flashing (locked to incoming MIDI clock), channel 3 pulsing, batched refresh via SysEx 03h with up to 81 colourspecs or RGB; enter Programmer mode on connect on the `LPMiniMK3 MIDI` interface and leave it on disconnect. MPD218: Note On/Off on the pad's own note, host-driven blink for armed. Ship two hardware-verified default profiles (Programmer bottom-left 4x4 and Drum-Rack 36 to 51 on channel 10) with instance slots. Knobs with rings get the current value where the profile's `capabilities` block declares rings (neither reference controller has them).

tasks.title: Test the two default mapping profiles in CI by replaying recorded controller byte logs
tasks.summary: Replay the raw MIDI byte logs the Phase 0 hardware verification recorded from the Launchpad Mini MK3 and the MPD218 through xj-control with each default profile on every PR, asserting the emitted cues, gestures and LED messages against a golden; this is how a mapping profile is tested in CI without a human, and it also guards the velocity-zero release rule and the name-resolution flags.

tasks.title: Emit MIDI clock from the BeatClock for non-Link gear and clocked LED blink
tasks.summary: A dedicated high-priority thread sends F8 at 24 ppqn from `time_at_beat(k/24)`, FA just before the downbeat's clock, FC/F2/FB for re-sync (Song Position Pointer wraps after 16,384 sixteenths, about 33 minutes at 124 bpm), through midir out, aiming at ±1 ms jitter. Also sent to any controller whose profile declares `blink = device` so the Launchpad's armed flash lands on the beat.

tasks.title: Implement the influence signals: control activity, room level over OSC, time in section
tasks.summary: Named smoothed floats that bias, never set: control activity (rate of mapped inputs over 8 bars nudges intensity up; silence hands back to the auto-crescendo), room level from an OSC float, and bars since the last Advance shown as a suggestion only. Off by default, bounded in magnitude, visible when on, logged for replay.

tasks.title: Compose wrapper, payload, decode, clock, voices and sink into a minimal play; hear a demo
tasks.summary: The R1 vertical slice before buses, FX, control, cues or variants exist: load Hero's Journey through xj-content, start the engine, decode and resample each referenced WAV on demand, convert run_cycle events to StartVoice/UpdateVoice/StopVoice at absolute device frames and play them through the cpal sink from a 100 ms control loop. Done when a maintainer hears the demo on all three OS and the late-command counter stays at zero for ten minutes.
proposal_refs: 03-architecture.md Data flow in one engine cycle

tasks.title: Implement the control-thread tick loop: cue scheduling, event conversion, snapshots
tasks.summary: At 10 to 20 Hz: read now in every base from the transport, apply pending cues whose landing falls within the craft-ahead window (the craft horizon, not the commit horizon; forwarding follow-mode refusals), call run_cycle, convert events to DSP commands, push them (plus SetMasterParams from the template config's thresholds and `mixerFiltersEnabled`, and the BeatClock tempo to the synced delay through SetFxParam), read the segment and message snapshot when changed (at most 10 Hz), publish an arc-swap snapshot for the UI. Craft runs inline on this thread; the 28 ms worst case leaves headroom. The published snapshot is the view-model defined in the Phase 0 fixture, so the Phase 3 surface draws the same shape it was prototyped against.
proposal_refs: 03-architecture.md Data flow in one engine cycle

tasks.title: Resolve pitch_shift and stretch requests on schedule events to pre-rendered variants
tasks.summary: When a schedule event carries `pitch_shift_semitones` or `stretch_ratio`, the station asks xj-content for the variant keyed by (content hash, ratio, semitones), preloads it ahead of the start frame on the I/O thread, and hands the voice the variant buffer; a variant that is not ready by its start frame falls back to the unshifted buffer and is counted. Tests cover a 5 percent stretch loop and a ±4 semitone shift against Signalsmith's clean range.

tasks.title: Ship xj-station play: the first shippable Rust binary that makes music from a V1 project
tasks.summary: `xj-station play <project.xj> --template <t> [--link] [--profile <toml>]` loads the project through xj-content, starts the engine, opens the device sink, attaches controllers and plays. `--link` selects the `link` BeatClock implementation (this is the station-side demonstration of the Phase 2 'Link integration behind a feature flag') and is present only in binaries built with `--features link`; a build without it rejects the flag with the Q3 fallback message (session clock plus MIDI clock out), and whichever clock is active drives or follows the engine tempo through the station's tempo wiring. This is the R1 slice: something musical ships before any UI exists. Includes `--list-devices`, `--buffer-frames` and a text status line with late and xrun counters.

tasks.title: Ship `xj-station render --minutes N` as a faster-than-real-time offline render
tasks.summary: Run the same runtime against the null sink and offline driver, writing the master (and optionally per-bus) WAVs through the segmented capture sink; exit non-zero on engine Error messages. Used by Ship-mode bounce, lint and CI.

tasks.title: Define the capture format: seed, chain dump, content lock, cue and gesture logs, audio
tasks.summary: A versioned capture directory whose header carries the engine version, the ABI version and the drawn chain seed, then: the sorted segment-store dump written incrementally per crafted segment (from `xj_engine_get_segments_json` through the serde snapshot types, in determinism mode omitting createdAt/updatedAt) so `replay` has a recorded chain to compare against, as 05-workstation's Capture ('starts recording the chain (segment store), the seed, the cue log and the bounced audio') requires; the content lock (project content hashes now, `show.lock` once shows exist), the cue log with beat timestamps and landing acknowledgements, the gesture and move log with device-frame timestamps, the influence log, the segmented bounced audio manifest, and a `CREDITS.md` slot. Written incrementally so a crash keeps what was recorded; the Phase 4 show task adds show.lock to the same header.

tasks.title: Ship `capture` and `replay`: replay reproduces the chain byte for byte and the mix
tasks.summary: `capture` wraps play with the capture format; `replay <capture>` re-runs the engine with the recorded seed and cue log and compares its sorted store dump byte for byte against the dump recorded in the capture (the comparison target is the capture's own chain dump, not a second live run), then replays the gesture log through the DSP into a render and reports the audio difference. A CI job captures then replays on every PR.

tasks.title: Implement TOML settings with Play-mode horizon defaults, logging, diagnostics bundle
tasks.summary: Settings in the platform config directory (audio host on Linux and device and buffer, controller profiles, horizons, paths); the horizons setting carries craft-ahead, dub-ahead, deadline and the commit horizon, and the station applies the Play-mode defaults of 04 §6 (commit horizon 1.0 beat, craft-ahead 8 s, dub-ahead 2 s) through `set_horizons()` whenever the template omits `commitHorizonBeats` and the station is not in Ship mode's bounce or Build, so every V1 project opened in Play mode reacts within a beat; an explicit template key or an explicit settings value overrides the default; `tracing` logs with the engine's log callback wired in; a diagnostics bundle (logs, engine messages, current content lock, last capture, system info) exportable from the CLI and later the Help menu, per Q11. A `diagnostics` setting turns the engine's choice diagnostics on through the ABI flag: on by default in Play mode and in the CLI, off for game hosts, which never pass through the station.

tasks.title: Measure gesture-to-audible, quantized-gesture and cue-to-audible latency against budget
tasks.summary: A loopback measurement of the 08-performer-input budget: unquantized gesture under 10 ms at 256 frames, beat-quantized gesture within one frame of the beat, intensity cue at the next beat, foundation cue at the chosen boundary and never sooner than the commit horizon. Publish the numbers per platform; they are the quantitative half of R3 before musicians judge the qualitative half in Phase 3.

tasks.title: Wire BeatClock tempo into the engine's External policy and engine tempo into the clock
tasks.summary: 07-session-protocol says tempo is owned by Link and the conductor's and followers' engines run with the tempo policy External so their foundation records carry the Link tempo; nothing in the station did that. When the active clock owns tempo (`link`, or `session` as a follower) the station sets `set_tempo_policy(External)` and forwards every `on_tempo` change that passes the 20 to 999 bpm rule to `set_external_tempo`; when the station owns tempo (the internal clock, or `session` as conductor) the policy stays Content and each new segment's tempo is pushed to the clock's `set_tempo` at the segment boundary. The pending external tempo and its landing boundary are published in the station snapshot for the header and the Phase 5 records. Done when a test on the internal clock shows a template tempo change reaching `tempo_bpm()` at the boundary, and a test with a scripted BeatClock shows a tempo nudge landing in the next crafted segment and nowhere earlier; the Link path itself is exercised later through the `link` feature.

tasks.title: Add `xj-station build`: Build for engine from the Phase 2 CLI, honoring principle 2
tasks.summary: 09 principle 2 says Build for engine exists from the first Rust workstation release, and the first Rust release is the Phase 2 CLI on `workstation-v2.0.0-alpha.N` tags. Add `xj-station build <project.xj> [--out build/]` over xj-content's Build for engine (48 kHz 16-bit stereo `<audioId>.wav` plus `build/<slug>.json`, skip-if-matching), with a progress line and a non-zero exit on any decode failure. Done when the alpha release notes list it and the Unreal importer accepts its output in the format-compatibility test.

tasks.title: Render the test project and Hero's Journey in CI and assert audio statistics
tasks.summary: A PR job that renders ten minutes of the engine test project and of Hero's Journey (0.6 GB, the only demo small enough to be a committed fixture; rendered from the CDN export `audio.xj.io/vgm.json`, the only demo export with lengthSeconds, with its hub-era `vgm-<uuid>.wav` keyed audio fetched from object storage, not from the GitHub repo JSON whose rewritten waveformKeys do not match the CDN, and not a 17.6 GB git clone; the fixture switches to the Hero's Journey pack when Phase 4 publishes it) and asserts no silence, no clipping, integrated loudness within a band, true peak at or below -1 dBTP, zero engine Error messages.

tasks.title: Schedule the 8-hour soak with dropout, late-command, xrun and memory assertions
tasks.summary: Nightly: `xj-station play` on the null sink with a simulated device clock and a scripted performer sending cues and gestures for eight hours; assert zero dropouts, zero late commands, zero xruns, bounded memory and cache size, and a valid segmented capture. Chain time past 36 minutes on Windows is exercised here. This null-sink soak is the regression proxy; the real-device evidence for the Phase 2 exit comes from the overnight run on maintainers' machines. The same nightly job also renders ten minutes of all four demos through the joined fixtures (repo JSON with `lengthSeconds`, CDN audio by id: Deep House with its delta arcs and 88.2 kHz audio, Lofi with its loop outliers, Ambient Flow and Hero's Journey) and asserts the per-PR render statistics on each, since only the two small fixtures render on every PR; this closes 09's 'offline render of the demo projects' before the Phase 2 gate.

tasks.title: Hold the Phase 2 A/B listening gate against the Java workstation and record the decision
tasks.summary: Maintainers play the same demo on the Java workstation and on `xj-station play` with a controller, blind where possible, and judge whether it sounds at least as good; record the decision (proceed to UI, or give the DSP another phase) with the latency numbers and soak results attached, per 09-roadmap's gate after Phase 2.

tasks.title: Run xj-station play eight hours on a real audio device on each OS before the Phase 2 gate
tasks.summary: The CI soak runs on the null sink and cannot observe device xruns or dropouts. On maintainers' machines (CoreAudio, WASAPI shared, PipeWire) run `xj-station play` for eight hours with the default profile, the device sink and a scripted performer, and collect the xrun, late-command and dropout counters plus the diagnostics bundle. Done when the three runs are attached to the gate record with zero dropouts, or the device-level hazard (R7) is filed.

tasks.title: Build render fixtures for the large demos: join repo JSON lengthSeconds to CDN audio by id
tasks.summary: The CDN exports bump_deep.json, slaps_lofi.json and space_flow.json carry no `lengthSeconds` and use the hub-era `{demo:true, projects:[...]}` shape, so rendering them directly would make every one-shot pick zero-length (DubWork.cpp:144-151 computes stop = start).
