Build a fixture generator that reads each demo's GitHub-repo JSON (which has `lengthSeconds` and the same audio ids), reads the CDN JSON with a small adapter of its own (the V1 reader never learns the hub-era shape) only to map audio id to CDN waveform key, and writes a build-layout payload whose keys resolve to the object-storage URLs, cached by hash; vgm.json already has `lengthSeconds` and keeps its direct path. Done when all four demos render ten minutes with drum content audible and the fixture generator runs in the nightly job before the render; the fixtures switch to the Commons packs when Phase 4 publishes them.

tasks.title: Release xj-station CLI binaries for three OS with checksums on pre-release tags
tasks.summary: cargo-dist (community-maintained, v0.33) on `workstation-v2.0.0-alpha.N` pre-release tags per the Phase 0 tag scheme: build on three OS (the binary carries `play`, `render`, `capture`, `replay` and `build`), publish archives with SHA-256 checksums and third-party notices from cargo-deny, pinned to engine-v2.0.0. Signing and notarization are set up in Phase 3 per R13, on top of this workflow; the overnight runs may use these alphas, while the CI soak and the gate build from source.

tasks.title: Write the one-page HLS sink design note that archives the Java ship path (Q9)
tasks.summary: Record the recovered design: PCM at the mixer format piped to a segmenter, media sequence derived from chain time (seq = floor(chainMicros / (1e6 * targetDuration))), 6 s target, EVENT playlist with HOLD-BACK of three segments plus ten seconds, strict in-order publication, playlist rehydration on restart, and the open encoder question (AAC licensing versus Opus or Vorbis in fMP4). A future `xj-ship-hls` crate can be written from it; nothing ships in 2.0.

tasks.title: Build the application shell: modes, navigation, settings, About, recents, window state
tasks.summary: In the Q1 toolkit: a window with Play, Make and Ship mode navigation, settings screens (audio device and buffer, MIDI devices, paths, horizons including the commit horizon in beats, shown with the Play-mode defaults and applied at the next segment boundary through `set_horizons()`, clock source (internal, `link` when built in, `session` in Phase 5) and the MIDI clock out port, crash-report toggle) over the station's TOML settings, an About panel with version and commit hash for bug reports, command-line open of a project (#463; file association is wired in packaging), recent projects, and window state. Make and Ship are placeholders that already show the running project.

tasks.title: Embed xj-station in the app with the snapshot stream and command channel
tasks.summary: The UI thread reads arc-swap snapshots at frame rate and the meter ring buffer, and sends commands (cues, gestures, settings) to the control thread through a channel; no mutex is shared. Mode switches never stop the music; content edits apply at the next segment boundary via `xj_engine_reload_content`.

tasks.title: Make the Make button open the project in the Java workstation and reload its saves
tasks.summary: Workstation 2.0.0 ships no editors and the Java workstation remains the editor of record, so 05's 'Make mode is one click away' is honored by launching the installed Java 1.9.x workstation on the current project (it accepts the path as its first command-line argument, #463) and watching the project files; a Java save is re-read by xj-content and applied through the engine's reload at the next segment boundary without stopping the music. Opening on the instrument playing now is a Phase 6 behavior and is noted as such in the tour.

tasks.title: Build the canvas surface component from the view-model and benchmark it on a 2019 laptop
tasks.summary: The performance surface is a canvas component in either toolkit (Canvas2D with a WebGL2 option in Tauri since WebKitGTK has no WebGPU; wgpu in iced), drawn from the Phase 0 snapshot view-model so the instrument is portable between hosts (R2). Benchmark sustained 60 fps with meters, animated chord strip and 200 timeline elements on the 2019 laptop and time-to-window under 2 s; fail CI on regression where a representative runner exists.

tasks.title: Make the whole surface drivable from the keyboard with screen-reader labels
tasks.summary: Every control reachable and operable from a laptop keyboard (the demo and fallback path), with focus order, shortcuts for scenes, palettes, boundary, advance, hold, capture, transport, the one-shot pads, bus gain, FX, stutter and fill (08: the whole surface is drivable from a laptop keyboard), and accessible names and states on every control. On iced this is new work; on Tauri it is ARIA on the DOM chrome plus an accessible overlay for the canvas. It waits for every surface element, the timeline and the controller panel so nothing it must reach is built after it.

tasks.title: Ship one scene pad with preview, landing time, audible Macro cue and the boundary picker
tasks.summary: The legibility pattern the whole surface repeats, built once end to end: a single pad that on hover or hold shows the engine's preview ('Fire, A minor, 124, lands in 2 bars') from `preview()` and `earliest_landing()`, on press sends a Macro cue at the selected boundary, and reflects armed and active states; beside it the cue-boundary selector (beat, bar, segment, section) with the landing time drawn on a stub harmony line. Done when the cue is audible at the displayed landing.

tasks.title: Build the 4x4 scenes grid and the palette rows with previews and content-aware greying
tasks.summary: One pad per macro program in the template laid out for a 4x4 controller, each with the preview and armed/active states of the one-pad slice; one palette row per taxonomy category, one button per meme, exclusive within a row, sending a Memes cue with preview, and greying choices that no content can satisfy (#341) by running `preview()` (xj_engine_preview_cue_json) for each palette button when the row is hovered or its content changes, at the cost of one scratch craft per button, cached until the next segment; no new introspection function is added.

tasks.title: Build the intensity control with ramp time and the influence indicator
tasks.summary: The one continuous control the engine already honors, now with a ramp time in beats, drawn with the influence bias when the influence layer is on, and the Energy value from the restored crescendo. The boundary selector lives in the one-pad slice.

tasks.title: Build the harmony strip with the commit-horizon line, landing marks and the chord picker
tasks.summary: Current and upcoming chords from the segment snapshot, the commit horizon drawn as a line, pending cue landings marked, 'lands in N bars' text. 'Cue chord' opens a picker that emits canonical chord names from the grammar port (free text would admit `CMaj7`, which the engine does not recognize) with an optional key, and sends a Chord cue.

tasks.title: Build the ten layer strips with meters, mute and solo as gesture plus cue, claim indicator
tasks.summary: One strip per instrument type with the bus meter, mute and solo buttons that send the bus gesture quantized to the surface's quantize choice (none, beat, bar; 08 §Gestures, and 07 §Layer's 'mutes at the next bar' for claims) through xj-control's routing, together with the Layer Mute cue, and a claim indicator placeholder the session panel fills in Phase 5.

tasks.title: Build Advance and Hold, Capture, and the transport header with the what-is-playing overlay
tasks.summary: Advance and Hold section cues; Capture start and stop writing the capture format; a header showing Link state, tempo, beat position and session placeholder; and the first-run 'what is playing' overlay naming macro program, key and tempo. Leave room on the header for the Link name and logo attribution Ableton's brand guideline will require, and a slot for the Phase 5 session status.

tasks.title: Show the pending external tempo with its landing boundary and the time-in-section hint
tasks.summary: While an External tempo is pending the header reads, for example, '124 to 126 at next segment (in 2 bars)' from the station snapshot's pending-tempo field (filled by the station's tempo wiring from the engine's tempo-landing message) and `earliest_landing(SEGMENT)`; beside Advance, 'N bars in this section' with a gentle overdue hint when the influence layer is on, suggesting only and never acting on its own. Done when a Link tempo change shows its landing before it takes effect and the hint appears after the configured bars.

tasks.title: Build on-screen gestures: one-shot pads with audio picker, bus gain, FX, stutter, fill
tasks.summary: 08-performer-input lists the on-screen surface as an input source where every control works by mouse or touch, and 05 says a controller maps onto the surface one-to-one, yet every gesture except bus mute and solo had only a controller mapping. Add a one-shot pad row whose pads pick an instrument or audio of the running template, a gain fader and four FX knobs (filter cutoff and resonance, delay time and feedback, reverb mix, saturation) on each layer strip, and Stutter and Fill buttons with their quantize option; each is routed through xj-control's gesture path so the same mapping drives screen and controller and every screen gesture is logged for replay. Done when a performance using only the mouse exercises every gesture in 08's table and the capture replays it.

tasks.title: Add Play-mode transport: start and stop the station, pick the template, restart the chain
tasks.summary: 05-workstation lists transport among the Play-mode elements and 03 gives start and stop to xj-transport, but no surface element started or stopped the station or chose the template the engine starts on (the CLI has `--template`). Add start and finish through the station with the trailing Delete events honored (voices release, no click), a template picker over `xj_engine_list_macro_programs_json` and the template introspection JSON, and a restart that reseeds the chain; the header shows the running state.

tasks.title: Build the timeline with pending-cue landing points and the diagnostics view
tasks.summary: Segments as blocks past to future with type, key, tempo, chords, memes and intensity, each choice with its program or instrument, delta windows when delta arcs are on, and the landing points of pending cues drawn where they will land. 200 elements at 60 fps from the snapshot. A diagnostics tab beside it shows warning and error messages by segment, per-stage craft timing, cue landing acknowledgements and collisions, and the late-command, xrun and (in Phase 5) late-record counters, with export to the diagnostics bundle.

tasks.title: Build the why panel over the choice diagnostics
tasks.summary: Clicking a choice lists the MarbleBag candidates, phases and weights (1 plus shared-meme count; phase 1 beats phase 2 absolutely) and the exclusions from both gates (meme stack, range, mute, barBeats mismatch, no audio for tones), read from the `xj.choice.*` SegmentMeta; the flag is set through the ABI's `diagnostics_enabled` create setting (or `xj_engine_set_diagnostics`) by the station's diagnostics setting, on by default in Play mode and off for game hosts.
proposal_refs: 05-workstation.md The timeline and the why panel

tasks.title: Build the controller panel: detected devices, default profile offer, instance slots
tasks.summary: List detected controllers with their resolved identity, offer the matching default profile on plug-in, assign instance slots when two identical devices appear, and show connection state from the rescan.

tasks.title: Build learn mode with LED preview and unresolved-name flags
tasks.summary: Touch a control, choose a cue, gesture, move or session action, see the LED states it will show, and write the profile; names that do not resolve against the loaded show are flagged inline.

tasks.title: Build the moves editor with relative timing and preview
tasks.summary: Compose steps of cues and gestures at beat, bar, segment or bar+N, bind the move to a control, preview the engine's cue previews and the gesture text, and save into the profile so moves travel with it.

tasks.title: Bundle the cleared interim starter as a V1 project with corrected loop metadata
tasks.summary: Bundle the interim starter the license decision allows: Hero's Journey (98 audios, Macro/Main only, the Unreal showcase) as a V1 project, restricted to the instruments the inventory classifies as original or cleared if the decision says so, with its 14 loop metadata fixes (loopBeats under-declared by an exact integer factor for 11 of them; the other three are files that are exactly 64 beats at 115 bpm declared at 95, so their fix is tempo 115 instead of 95) applied once here and consumed by the Phase 4 pack. Show the license text the decision chose and the credits on first run; the swap to the commissioned CC0 starter pack is a Phase 4 task.

tasks.title: Build the launch-to-sound pipeline and measure it under 10 s on a 2019 laptop
tasks.summary: Open the window in under 2 s, load the starter (the largest demo loads in about 110 ms and starts in 60 ms, so the budget is decoding and UI), preload the first dub window, start the device and show the overlay; sound within 10 s of launch on the 2019 laptop, measured on every release candidate and once in CI on a representative runner.

tasks.title: Build the three-step first-run tour with previews and a controller prompt
tasks.summary: Press a scene pad, drag intensity, press a palette button, each showing its preview before it lands; then prompt to plug in a controller and show Make mode one click away (it opens the Java editor on the project; opening on the playing instrument is Phase 6). Follow #309's checklist (welcome, 'don't show again', skip) with 'starter pack already here' replacing 'clone a demo'. Steps 4 and 5 of the first run (plug in a controller and get a default layout; Make mode one click away) are reached from the tour's last screen.

tasks.title: Decide the redistribution license of the interim starter content before it ships in 2.0.0
tasks.summary: The demos carry no content license and include third-party library samples, so bundling Hero's Journey into a signed installer is the same redistribution act as publishing a pack. With counsel and the Phase 0 inventory, the company decides whether Hero's Journey (or the subset the inventory classifies as original or cleared) may be bundled and under which license text is shown on first run, or substitutes rights-clear or CC0 interim material, possibly a reduced set. Recorded as an ADR that p4-seed-rights-clearance-decision later extends to all four demos.

tasks.title: Add a Play-mode template and station defaults to the interim starter for usability
tasks.summary: The usability program judges R3 on the interim starter, so it must not run on the game template's defaults. Add a template variant with commitHorizonBeats = 1.0 and shorter main sequences, keeping the game template for Ship mode; the station's Play-mode defaults (one-beat commit horizon, craft-ahead 8 s, dub-ahead 2 s) already apply through the settings task when a template omits the key, so this variant exists for the shorter sequences and so the template itself documents the horizon it was tuned for. Done when a Bar-boundary Macro cue on it lands within one bar plus the one-beat horizon (at most 5 beats, median at most 4) at 95, 115, 135 and 120 bpm, and Build for engine of the starter omits it so the Unreal plugin never plays it.

tasks.title: Build the Ship-mode Build for engine and bounce screens
tasks.summary: Build for engine with the pinned output contract and a dirtiness indicator from content hashes (not 'any edit' as in V1); bounce with template selection, minutes and progress over the offline render.

tasks.title: Build capture export with audio and data and a CREDITS.md slot
tasks.summary: Export a capture as its segmented audio plus the data files, leaving the capture format's CREDITS.md slot for the Phase 4 generator (V1 entities carry no author or license field, so there is nothing to generate credits from until pack manifests exist); the interim starter's license text from the first-run decision is copied in as a placeholder.

tasks.title: Produce installable bundles for macOS universal, Windows and Linux
tasks.summary: DMG with a universal binary (arm64 plus x86_64, macOS 12+), NSIS and MSI (Windows 10 21H2+ x64), AppImage plus .deb (glibc 2.35+), through tauri-bundler or the toolkit's bundler; bundle the starter project, default profiles and third-party notices. Register the `.xj` file association (#326); `.xjpack` is registered in Phase 4 when the pack reader exists. Official Windows builds leave the `asio` feature off until Steinberg countersigns; when it is enabled, CI fetches the SDK at build time and never vendors it.

tasks.title: Extend the signing and notarization pipeline from the CLI to the app bundles
tasks.summary: Apple Developer ID signing with hardened runtime and notarytool, Windows code signing of installer and binaries, Linux signatures and checksums, all from the pipeline built in Phase 2; verify installs on clean machines of each platform.

tasks.title: Set up the auto-update channel with signed manifests and the post-advisory updater
tasks.summary: tauri-plugin-updater >= 2.12.0 (CVE-2026-95624 and CVE-2026-95625) with the signed-version option, minisign keys generated and held under documented custody (losing the key strands installs), a static manifest endpoint over TLS, Windows installMode, and the knowledge that only AppImage, .app.tar.gz, NSIS and MSI are updatable. On the iced path, an equivalent in-house updater with the same signature scheme.

tasks.title: Add opt-in crash reporting and the Help-menu diagnostics bundle per Q11
tasks.summary: sentry 0.49 with the `minidump` feature for native crashes, pointed at a self-hosted GlitchTip or the Sentry free tier; disable the default `logs`, `metrics` and `release-health` features so no usage telemetry leaves the machine; off by default with a visible toggle and a plain description; export the diagnostics bundle from Help.

tasks.title: Release XJ music workstation 2.0.0 once the Phase 3 exit and gate are met
tasks.summary: Tag `workstation-v2.0.0` when launch-to-sound is measured under 10 s, the usability sessions are filed and the gate decision is recorded, Ship mode and the docs are complete, and the update channel works from a previous build.

tasks.title: Enable the link feature in official builds and add Link attribution once licensed
tasks.summary: File the countersigned grant and record fee, attribution requirements, and whether it covers the headless runtime, all three OS builds and the binding fork as the Q3 ADR. Turn `--features link` on in the workstation and CLI release workflows, update the fork's license file to the proprietary grant's terms with the `LicenseRef-Ableton-Link-Proprietary` identifier and move it from the developer-only GPL exception to the official allow list in cargo-deny; add the Link name and logo per Ableton's brand guideline to the header slot, a Settings entry and the docs. If Ableton declines, record the fallback (session clock plus MIDI clock out) as the Q3 decision and drop `--link` from shipped help.

tasks.title: Enable the asio feature in official Windows builds once Steinberg countersigns (Q10)
tasks.summary: File the countersigned agreement, record the date in the Q10 ADR, and turn `asio` on in the Windows release job with CI fetching the SDK at build time (never vendored). Add the README note on the Third-Party Modified Version clause (forks need their own agreement) and the no-'ASIO'-in-product-names rule. If the agreement is never countersigned, record the WASAPI-only stance (Audacity's position) as the decision.

tasks.title: Decide Windows on ARM support once a test machine exists and record it in the Q10 ADR
tasks.summary: 11-resolutions Q10 leaves 'Confirming Windows on ARM once there is a machine to test on' open and the Phase 0 record ships x64 only. On a Windows-on-ARM machine, test the x64 NSIS/MSI installer under emulation (audio device, MIDI, latency) and a native aarch64 build of the workstation; decide ship, ship-emulated or defer, record it as an amendment to the Q10 ADR, and update the platform table in 05 and 11 through the decisions index.

tasks.title: Write the usability session protocol and recruit five musicians new to XJ
tasks.summary: Protocol: a musician who has never seen XJ, a pad controller, the tour, then 20 minutes of performing; measure time to first intentional cue, where the landing-time honesty helps or frustrates (R3), confusion points, and what they ask for (R12 scope creep is logged, not promised). Recruit five, at least two on macOS.

tasks.title: Have a musician new to XJ perform twenty minutes with a pad controller after the tour
tasks.summary: The Phase 3 exit's second clause as its own demonstration: a musician who has never seen XJ takes the tour with a Launchpad or MPD218 and performs for twenty minutes; the keyboard-and-mouse fallback path is demonstrated too, including the on-screen gestures; the capture is kept as data, the facilitator notes every moment the performer looked for something the surface did not show, and the result is filed before the five sessions run.

tasks.title: Run the five usability sessions on release candidates
tasks.summary: Run and record the sessions against release-candidate builds with the two default profiles, the tour, the harmony strip and the why panel; a facilitator and a note-taker per session; collect the capture of each performance as data.

tasks.title: File the findings as issues and record the post-Phase-3 gate decision
tasks.summary: Every finding becomes a labeled issue; the decision record answers 'do musicians want to play it', sets the scope of Phase 5 and the shape of Phase 6, and rules on R3's next lever (shrinking segments in Play mode is content work, not engine work) if latency disappointed.

tasks.title: Write the Play-mode performer's guide
tasks.summary: Scenes, palettes, intensity, boundaries and landing times, the harmony strip and chord picker, layers, the on-screen gestures (one-shot pads, bus gain, FX, stutter, fill), transport and template choice, advance and hold, timeline and why panel, capture, settings and diagnostics; with the three-scale model (direction, articulation, gesture) explained in the performer's words.

tasks.title: Write the mapping TOML reference and document the two default profiles
tasks.summary: Every table and key of the profile format, the tiered match key and why manufacturer/product globs are not available, the default-boundary table per cue type when `boundary` is omitted, LED states per controller, moves syntax, and the Launchpad Mini MK3 and MPD218 defaults with their note layouts.

tasks.title: Write the 2.0.0 installation pages and the Ship-mode guide (build, bounce, capture export)
tasks.summary: docs.xjmusic.com's installation/ pages (linux, mac-intel, mac-silicon, windows) and getting-started/ (menu bar 'clone a demo', fabrication tab) describe the Java 1.9.x installers and UI. Write the 2.0.0 installation pages for the three bundles (DMG universal, NSIS/MSI, AppImage/.deb; auto-update; the `.xj` association), a getting-started page that follows the first-run tour ('starter pack already here', Make mode opens the Java editor until Phase 6), and the Ship-mode guide: Build for engine with the pinned output contract and the dirtiness indicator, bounce, capture export and the CREDITS.md slot. The Java editor pages stay for 1.9.x, marked as such, until the Phase 6 migration guide replaces them.

tasks.title: Define pack.toml, show.toml and show.lock schemas and open V1 projects as implicit packs
tasks.summary: serde schemas for `[pack]` (name, version, title, authors, license as a validated SPDX id (required; share-alike and non-commercial family identifiers rejected; CC BY 4.0 default, CC0 allowed, per 06 Licensing and Q6), description, tags, engine range, taxonomy), `[taxonomy] palettes` in `CATEGORY[A, B, C]` syntax, `[dependencies]`, `[provenance]`; `show.toml` (`[show]`, `[packs]`, `[session]` with taxonomy, commit_horizon_beats, follow_hold_max_bars) and `show.lock` (`[[pack]]` name, version, hash). A V1 project opens as a pack with an implicit manifest.

tasks.title: Implement the .xjpack layout with BLAKE3 audio names, a format sidecar and provenance
tasks.summary: `content/libraries/**` and `content/templates/**` in the V1 shape, `audio/<blake3>.<ext>` with `InstrumentAudio.contentHash` as the link and the original `waveformKey` kept for display, a per-audio format sidecar `audio/<blake3>.toml` (a register deviation, listed in the rationale) recording sample rate, bit depth, channels, encoding and frames read from the WAV headers (the demos span 44.1 to 96 kHz, 16/24-bit PCM and 32-bit float, mono and stereo), `originPack`/`originVersion` on every entity so forks trace to their source, and `preview/render.ogg` optional. Two audios sharing one key with different hashes is an error. An optional `mapping/` folder carries controller profiles and moves (in the Phase 2 mapping TOML format) so they are shareable as part of a pack. A pack is a directory or a zip of one: the reader opens either without asking, including an OS-opened `.xjpack`, with a round-trip test zip to directory to zip preserving every hash.

tasks.title: Implement pack dependencies: semver ranges, cross-pack bindings, duplicate-id precedence
tasks.summary: A template in one pack may bind programs and instruments from a dependency; resolve `[dependencies]` ranges, define precedence when the same UUID appears in two packs (the engine collapses duplicates silently, last file wins), reject duplicate ids within one pack, and recognize the same program by `originPack`/`originVersion`. Packs are immutable once published.

tasks.title: Implement `xj-content pack`: hash audio, read headers, map keys, write the manifest
tasks.summary: Build a pack from a V1 project or an open project: hash every audio, write the `audio/<blake3>.toml` format sidecar from WAV headers, map waveform keys, and generate pack.toml from project metadata with prompts for license and authors; the lint task wires `pack` to invoke lint once it exists (06: 'hashes audio, writes the manifest, lints'). Handles the Build-output layout (`<audioId>.ext` keys) and the libraries/ layout as inputs.

tasks.title: Implement the structural lint rules and the ten-minute render check
tasks.summary: Wire `pack` to run this lint after writing the manifest. Manifest validates, including a valid semver range in `engine`; license is an SPDX id, share-alike and non-commercial family identifiers are rejected, CC BY 4.0 is the default and CC0 is allowed; every hash matches; no duplicate ids; enum strings are the ten types, three modes, four program types (the engine degrades unknown values silently to Drum/Event/Main); config strings parse with the C++ ConfigParser subset (no comments, substitutions, path keys or nested objects; `1` versus `1.0` typing); no `isDeleted` or Draft entity reachable from a shipped template; no dangling `waveformKey`; `lengthSeconds` equals the decoded frame count. A README.md must be present and say what the pack is for. Given a show.toml, lint additionally checks that every resolved pack's `taxonomy` equals `[session].taxonomy`, naming the pack that differs. Then render ten minutes on each template through the null sink with zero engine Error messages.

tasks.title: Implement the musical lint rules: note coverage, loop length, taxonomy drift, chords
tasks.summary: Event and Chord instruments cover the note range their templates' voicings demand (derived from `NoteRange::ofStrings` of voicings per type, since V1 content declares no range) or set allowPitchShift with a range; every Loop audio's length agrees with loopBeats × 60 / tempo within 1 percent, else diagnose (integer multiple means fix loopBeats; whole beats at another declared tempo means fix tempo; else trim) and refuse allowStretch while any loop fails; memes are xj-base conventions or members of a declared palette, every declared category is used, palette-like memes are declared, case variants (`EARTH`/`Earth`) are flagged, and the same word in two packs' categories with different meanings fails; chord descriptions outside the 41 canonical forms, atonal program keys (UUIDs, `c`) and lowercase `x` tones warn with fixes.

tasks.title: Implement the loudness rule with ebur128 on the effective level, Phase 0 calibrated
tasks.summary: Classify audio as sustained (Loop mode or at least 3 s) or one-shot; measure sustained audio with BS.1770-4 integrated loudness via `ebur128`, one-shots by max momentary loudness (zero-padding under 400 ms, since integrated returns -inf) and true peak; measure in the playback channel layout; compute the effective level by adding 20·log10(audio.volume × instrument.volume) because a third of demo audio relies on non-unity volume; true peak at or below -1.0 dBTP for every file. The statistics helpers (silence, clipping, integrated loudness via ebur128, true peak) are the ones the golden render tests ship. The target (proposal -18 LUFS ±3 LU, or the demo median) is the one the Phase 0 baseline measurement calibrated and xj-base@1 published; this task implements it and ships `--report`, whose run on the four demos confirms the calibration rather than setting it.

tasks.title: Implement `xj-content render` producing preview/render.ogg as Ogg Vorbis with tags
tasks.summary: There is no maintained pure-Rust Vorbis encoder and symphonia has no Opus decoder, so render the 60 to 120 s preview with `vorbis_rs` (libvorbis aoTuV via `cc`) at QualityVbr 0.4 at the render's native rate, planar f32 blocks of 1024, with comments TITLE, ARTIST, LICENSE, XJ_PACK, XJ_TEMPLATE, XJ_ENGINE, XJ_LOUDNESS_LUFS and XJ_TRUE_PEAK_DBTP; reserve `render.opus` in the schema. Decode-verify with symphonia.

tasks.title: Implement `xj-content publish`: sign, upload the artifact, open the index pull request
tasks.summary: Sign with the author key, zip and upload to R2 by content hash, and open a PR on xjmusic/commons adding the index entry with the manifest, hash, public key on first publish, the contributor declaration (reviewed text) and the hours log that the equity rule needs. No server-side accounts.

tasks.title: Implement `fetch --show` and `lock`: resolve, download via mirrors, verify, write the lock
tasks.summary: Resolve `[packs]` semver ranges against the index, download artifacts by hash trying mirrors in order (registry, venue NAS, USB directory, local cache), verify, unpack each downloaded artifact into the local mirror through the pack reader's zip path, check each pack's `engine` range (and the show's resolved set) against the running engine and ABI versions (`xj_abi_version`, asserted at startup by xj-engine-sys) and refuse with the pack and the range named, and write `show.lock`; `lock` re-resolves and rewrites. The workstation keeps a local mirror of every pack fetched so a venue needs no internet once its show is fetched; `fetch` on one machine plus a USB stick is a supported path.

tasks.title: Create the xjmusic/commons index repository and the R2 artifact bucket
tasks.summary: A repository holding `/index/<name>.json` published via Pages or raw, with README, CODEOWNERS, a PR template carrying the hours log (Q5) with fields for the author's hours, the reviewers' listening hours and a cap note the reviewers fill in when they judge the log implausible, and git history as the audit log; an R2 bucket behind a custom domain with hash-addressed keys and CORS for the later browser audition; mirrors are a `git clone` plus any bucket copy.

tasks.title: Implement pack signing with minisign keys, author binding, maintainer keys and verify
tasks.summary: Use the `minisign` crate (0.10; it does not depend on ed25519-dalek) for pack signatures with trusted and untrusted comments; the index records the author's public key on first publish and later versions must be signed by the same key or a maintainer key; document key generation, custody and revocation. Keep this pin separate from the Tauri updater's minisign 0.9, which has broken signatures on bumps. `xj-content verify <pack>` checks the signature against the author key recorded in the index on first publish or a maintainer key, and every audio and content hash; usable offline against a mirror.

tasks.title: Build the index repository CI: verify signature, lint, render preview, upload, then merge
tasks.summary: On each publish PR: verify the signature against the recorded key, run the full lint, render and attach the preview, upload the artifact to R2, record the declarer and hours log, and merge the index entry only when all pass; two maintainers' listening approvals are a required review. Packs are immutable once published (06): CI rejects any change to an existing `<name>@<version>` entry or its recorded hash (a new version is required), refuses an artifact whose content hash already exists under another name or version, and allows yanking a version only with the maintainer key.

tasks.title: Write the pack authoring and publishing guide, the lint reference and the licensing page
tasks.summary: docs.xjmusic.com: how to author, lint, preview and publish a pack; every lint rule with its fix; the immutability rule (a published version never changes, a fix is a new version, yanking is a maintainer action); the three things that are licensed (software, Commons content, output) kept apart; CC BY attribution made automatic via CREDITS.md; the contributor declaration; and the contributing section states the two Q5 guardrails from the company decision record: hours are logged per pack in the publish PR and may be capped at review time if the reviewers judge the log implausible, and reviewing hours count for the maintainers who listen. Remove CONFIDENTIALITY.md from the public repositories as part of this cleanup.

tasks.title: Run the exit demonstration: an external contributor publishes a pack that passes lint
tasks.summary: Recruit a musician outside the core team, have them author and publish a pack following the guide alone, record every friction point as an issue, and merge their pack into the index through the same PR flow; it does not wait for the seed packs' listening review, since the publish CI and the guide are its only producers.

tasks.title: Compose a show's template: taxonomy union, horizon settings, one template per station
tasks.summary: Union the packs' `[taxonomy] palettes` into the structured `memeTaxonomy` list-of-objects form the C++ TemplateConfig parses (not the compact `;`-separated string), apply `commit_horizon_beats` and `follow_hold_max_bars` from `[session]`, resolve `pack/Template` references to template ids before the engine sees them, and produce exactly one template per station: a show.toml lists several templates, show composition resolves `pack/Template` to one template id per station, and the engine is started on that template. Composition refuses a show whose packs cite a different xj-base version from `[session].taxonomy` (06 §A shared taxonomy: packs combine only if their memes mean the same thing), naming the pack and both versions; the same check runs in the structural lint over a show manifest. The show's `[session]` commit_horizon_beats and follow_hold_max_bars are applied to the composed template's config so every station runs the same horizon settings.

tasks.title: Make xj-station load a show from a verified lockfile, local mirror or USB path, tested
tasks.summary: `xj-station play --show show.toml` resolves show.lock, verifies every pack hash against the local mirror, checks every pack's `engine` range against the running engine and ABI versions (refusing with a reason that the pack browser shows), composes the show template and starts; a registry that is unreachable is never an error when the mirror is complete. Integration tests fetch a show through a mirror list with the registry down, from a directory mirror and from a USB-style path, verifying hashes, and prove that a station with a complete local mirror needs no network. This is the venue workflow 06 names.

tasks.title: Prove two machines with the same lockfile load byte-identical content
tasks.summary: A fixture pack is published to the registry through `xj-content publish` by the job itself (so nothing is uploaded by hand), then CI on two runners fetches the same show from the registry with the same lock and compares content hashes, composed template configs and the engine's introspection JSON; this is half of the Phase 4 exit demonstration.

tasks.title: Record show.lock, engine and ABI versions in the capture header and verify them on replay
tasks.summary: When a show is loaded the capture header carries show.lock (pack names, versions, hashes), the engine version, the ABI version, the workstation version and the mapping-profile hash, completing the content-lock half the Phase 2 format left open (the chain dump, engine version, ABI version and seed are already in the Phase 2 header). `replay` refuses on a lock mismatch and warns on a version mismatch. Done when a capture replayed on a second machine with the same lock reproduces the chain and one with a different lock is refused with the differing pack named.

tasks.title: Publish xj-base@1 as a versioned document including the loudness rule and meme grammar
tasks.summary: Version the reviewed draft at xj-base@1: tempo, density, size, structure and character conventions, the meme grammar, the per-pack declared palettes rule, the sanitize constraints, and the loudness and true-peak rule with its provenance (R 128 s1, ASWG-R001) and the demo calibration note. Packs cite it in `taxonomy = "xj-base@1"`.

tasks.title: Have counsel review the contributor declaration and the CC BY/CC0 license interaction
tasks.summary: Counsel reviews the declaration text ('I own or have cleared every sample in this pack'), how a CC BY 4.0 pack satisfies the software license's 'you own the rights to the input audio' provision for output audio, and the share-alike and non-commercial exclusions; adopt the wording in the CLI and the index PR template. Closes Q6.

tasks.title: Generate CREDITS.md into every capture, bounce, build and exported pack
tasks.summary: From the pack manifests of the loaded show: each pack's authors, license and link, in a reasonable-manner attribution block; written by the capture format, the offline render, Build for engine and Export pack.

tasks.title: Obtain the rights decision for relicensing demo audio and clear or replace samples
tasks.summary: With the Phase 0 inventory and counsel's declaration wording, obtain the company's decision to release the demos under CC BY 4.0 (or CC0), review each instrument whose provenance is a third-party library against that library's license, and replace anything that cannot be redistributed. Record the decision; no demo pack is published before it.

tasks.title: Build the Hero's Journey pack from the corrected interim project: palettes, preview
tasks.summary: The smallest demo (98 audios, 0.6 GB, Macro/Main only, two palette rows, already the Unreal showcase) becomes the first pack: pack the corrected project (the 14 loop metadata fixes from gap-demo-audio-facts §3: loopBeats multiplied by the exact factor, and tempo 115 instead of 95 on the three 64-beat loops; were made in Phase 3 if the interim-starter decision shipped Hero's Journey; if it substituted other material, apply the 14 fixes here, once), declare ACTION and HEROSJOURNEY palettes, pack, lint, render the preview, and publish it through `xj-content publish` as the first index PR.

tasks.title: Build the Lofi Hip Hop and Deep House packs: loop fixes, lost samples, case variants
tasks.summary: Lofi: fix the 18 Loop audios left at the inherited default loopBeats of 4.0 or 8.0, restore the one kick sample that a waveform-key collision overwrote in the demo repository (the original is still on audio.xj.io), review the 220 audios whose tempo is the 120 default in a 75/85 bpm project, declare the CITY palette. Deep House: restore the one Sticky sample lost to the same collision, fix the three loop outliers, normalize `EARTH`/`Earth` and `BREAK`/`Break` case variants, remove the Hero's Journey vocabulary copied onto programs, declare ELEMENT, and push 4.5 GB of mostly 88.2 kHz audio through the resampler; it is the only template with delta arcs on, so it is the delta-arc fixture. Pack, lint, preview both, subject to the rights-clearance decision.

tasks.title: Build the Ambient Flow pack: resolve the unused SEASON palette and publish 15.8 GB
tasks.summary: The template declares SEASON but no content uses it, while SAVORY/SPICY/SWEET/SOUR and fruit memes do: declare the palettes actually used or tag content, pass the drift lint, and publish the 927 audios (71 percent of all demo bytes, all 48 kHz 24-bit) to the bucket; 118 s pads make this the long-segment fixture for cue boundaries.

tasks.title: Commission and build the CC0 starter pack that ships with the workstation
tasks.summary: Commissioned, not crowdsourced, so first-launch quality is not left to chance: a CC0 pack built from the best demo material or new material, tagged against xj-base@1, with a template tuned for Play mode (short segments, one-beat horizon), passing lint and the loudness rule, with a preview. Its adoption as the engine CI fixture is its own task.

tasks.title: Hold the two-maintainer listening review per seed pack and mark the CDN export legacy
tasks.summary: Two maintainers listen to each preview and a ten-minute live render with intensity swept check that the README says what the pack is for and what it is not for, and approve in the index PR; then mark `audio.xj.io/{shipKey}.json` as the legacy 1.9.x demo source (three of the four lack lengthSeconds and use the hub-era shape) and point docs at the packs.

tasks.title: Adopt the starter pack as an engine fixture; re-time craft per stage on the largest pack
tasks.summary: Switch the Phase 2 CI render job from the CDN vgm.json export to the Hero's Journey pack, and check the starter pack's engine payload into the engine test data as the fixture for the follow-mode and determinism tests (alongside the richer fixture), and run the in-tree timing harness on the largest Commons pack (Deep House) in the CI bench job, recording per-stage craft timing from the Phase 1 timing messages. Done when the harness table for the pack is attached to the Phase 4 release notes and the commit-horizon contingency decision is re-confirmed or reopened.

tasks.title: Build the pack browser and show fetch with license display and a CREDITS.md preview
tasks.summary: Browse the index, preview packs (play `preview/render.ogg`: decoded by symphonia's vorbis path on the I/O thread and played through the running DSP graph as a `TriggerOneShot` on a dedicated audition voice routed to Master, the same path the Phase 6 editor audition reuses; no second cpal stream is opened, and the audition stops when the browser closes), build or open a show, fetch with progress through the mirror list, show lock state and offline readiness. Each pack's license, authors and link from the manifest are shown before it is added to a show, CC0 marked as obligation-free, with a CREDITS.md preview for the current show.

tasks.title: Build Ship-mode Export pack with lint report and preview render
tasks.summary: From the open project: run `pack`, show the lint report inline with fixes, render the preview, and write the .xjpack; publishing hands off to the CLI flow with the declaration.

tasks.title: Bundle the CC0 starter pack in place of the interim project and release workstation 2.1
tasks.summary: Bundle the commissioned starter pack once its two-maintainer listening review is approved, remove the interim V1 project, register the `.xjpack` file association (an OS-opened pack, directory or zip, opens through the pack reader), re-measure launch to sound on the 2019 laptop, update the tour text and credits display, and tag `workstation-v2.1.0` when the byte-identical show test passes, an external contributor has published, and Export pack and license display work.

tasks.title: Write and publish the versioned JSON Schema for all session messages and the epoch
tasks.summary: hello, welcome, reject, foundation, retract, claim, release, cue_request, cue_result, handoff_offer, handoff_accept, handoff_commit, presence, bye, each with a `type` field, length-prefixed framing, a protocol version, the `welcome` epoch as (conductor bar identity, conductor Link-clock micros at that downbeat, barBeats) per the Phase 0 decision, the conductor's show.lock embedded in `welcome` and in the lock-mismatch `reject`, and the foundation record reusing the engine schema plus `session` and `seq`. Published on the docs site.

tasks.title: Publish message fixtures and a minimal reference reader for non-XJ participants
tasks.summary: A fixture set covering every message and failure path, and a tiny read-only client (Python or JavaScript) that joins as an observer and prints the harmonic timeline, proving the 'a lighting desk can read it' promise.

tasks.title: Implement mDNS discovery of `_xjsession._tcp` with a join code and a manual-IP fallback
tasks.summary: The conductor advertises the session name and a four-character code via mdns-sd (own daemon thread, self-described beta, no unicast responses), followers browse; because venue networks mishandle multicast, a typed IP and port always works. The code prevents joining the wrong stage, not attackers.

tasks.title: Implement QUIC with self-signed certs trusted via the join code, with TCP fallback
tasks.summary: quinn needs certificates: the conductor generates a self-signed cert with rcgen and the follower verifies it against a fingerprint derived with the join code (trust on first use); one connection per follower, length-prefixed JSON messages, TCP fallback when QUIC is blocked. A transport trait lets the test harness substitute an in-memory or lossy transport.

tasks.title: Implement hello, welcome, reject, presence and bye with lock and version checks (16 max)
tasks.summary: hello carries station id, name, engine and ABI versions, join code and the show.lock hash; welcome carries session id, epoch, member list, current claims, the next few foundation records and the conductor's show.lock (pack names, versions, hashes), as 06 says the conductor sends the lock; reject names the reason (bad code, version mismatch, lock mismatch) for the UI, and the lock-mismatch reject carries the same show.lock so a follower with a stale or missing lock can fetch the show and rejoin. A follower may not follow until its content is byte-identical. The conductor rejects a seventeenth station. Periodic presence carries state, round-trip estimate and a meters summary; bye is the clean departure; after a timeout a vanished follower's claims are released and everyone un-mutes those layers at the next segment.

tasks.title: Publish sequenced foundation records, consume them in follow mode, retract on rewrite
tasks.summary: Every follower's engine runs with the tempo policy External through the station's tempo wiring; the conductor's runs External only when the active BeatClock owns tempo (`link`, 07 §Clock's Link-room case) and Content otherwise (the `session` clock this task is built on, where the conductor's segment tempo drives the clock), so each record carries the session tempo in both cases. The conductor reads `xj_engine_get_foundation_json` after each craft, wraps it with session and seq, and broadcasts; followers push records into `push_foundation_json` translated through the epoch (conductor bar identity plus conductor clock micros, mapped with the session clock's offset estimate; Link is not required); when a cue rewrites the conductor's future it sends retract(from segment N) and republishes. Followers discard retracted records they have not crafted against; retracts inside a follower's horizon are impossible by construction. Built first as two stations in one process over an in-memory transport, reusing the Rust follow test, then over the LAN connection; this is the protocol's own two-engines test.

tasks.title: Compute the effective commit horizon and hold one segment on a late record, counted
tasks.summary: The conductor's effective horizon is its own commitHorizonBeats plus every follower's dub-ahead (reported in hello and presence); the conductor refuses or defers cues inside it and shows it; followers' craft horizons derive from the conductor's in welcome and are applied through `set_horizons()` at the join boundary, so no engine is recreated and no audio drops. Solo stations react at the next beat, sessions at the next bar, and the UI says so. A foundation record that arrives too late to craft against makes the follower hold for that one segment, log a warning and increment a late-record counter exposed in the snapshot for the UI and the soak assertions.

tasks.title: Implement layer claims and releases that mute other stations' layers via cue and gesture
tasks.summary: claim/release flow through the conductor to all; every other station's engine receives a Layer Mute cue for that type at the next segment and its bus mutes at the next bar; release reverses both; a station may override locally ('doubling allowed') and the UI shows the clash; the default two-station claim set (A: Drum and Bass) ships as a preset.

tasks.title: Forward followers' foundation cues as cue requests under accept-all, trust list, ask mode
tasks.summary: A follower's engine refuses Macro, Memes, Chord, Advance and Hold with the follow-mode status; the station forwards a cue_request; the conductor applies the policy (accept all with the sender shown by default per Q13, a named trust list, or ask the conductor's performer) and returns cue_result with the landing time, which the requester shows exactly like a local cue. Collisions at one boundary apply in arrival order and are shown.

tasks.title: Implement the three-step conductor handoff at a segment boundary
tasks.summary: handoff_offer names the candidate and the earliest segment beyond the conductor's horizon and the candidate's craft lead; handoff_accept confirms the candidate can conduct from there; handoff_commit names the segment, at which the candidate switches foundation source External to Internal and publishes a NextMacro segment while the old conductor switches Internal to External, both through the station's boundary switch (the one producer, from the station integration task) so audio is continuous. Everyone else sees a new sender on the same timeline; epoch continuity is preserved.

tasks.title: Test every row of the failure table end to end on the simulated-network harness
tasks.summary: The rows are implemented by their owners (late record: the horizon handshake; claim release after a follower timeout and the version or lock mismatch reject at hello: the session transport task; conductor vanishes: the engine's hold, fallback and rejoin plus the station's boundary switch; Link peers vanish: the Link clock keeps the last tempo). This task injects each row on the simulated-network harness (conductor killed mid-segment, follower killed holding claims, records delayed past the horizon, a stale lock, a mismatched version), asserts the specified outcome and timing for each, and verifies that every outcome is logged into the capture and shown in the diagnostics view with the counter the UI task reads. Done when the table in 07 has one green test per row.

tasks.title: Wire xj-session into the xj-station loop and CLI: host, join, role, boundary switch
tasks.summary: Network I/O (connect, hello/welcome, foundation publish/consume, claims, cue requests, presence) runs on the tokio I/O thread that owns the QUIC/TCP connection (03 §Threads: xj-session is event-driven and may block on disk and network); messages cross to the control thread through a channel and are applied at the 10 to 20 Hz tick, so a blocking connect or a slow peer never stalls craft or cue scheduling, and nothing touches the audio thread. CLI flags: `--session <name>` or `--connect <ip:port>`, `--join-code`, `--role conduct|follow`; a headless conductor prints and serves its join code. Joining switches the engine's foundation source Internal to External at the conductor-aligned NextMacro boundary while audio keeps playing; leaving reverses the switch at a segment boundary and sends `bye`. Done when a test asserts zero dropouts and zero late commands across a join and a leave of a running station.

tasks.title: Implement the conductor-hosted session BeatClock with NTP-style offset estimation
tasks.summary: Followers estimate their offset to the conductor with round trips over the session connection (filtered, outlier-rejected), and the conductor's beat timeline is the truth; the trait methods from Phase 2 are implemented over it; MIDI clock out from Phase 2 runs on it for non-Link hardware through the trait, without this task depending on the emitter. This is the CI clock and the Q3 fallback. The station's tempo wiring sets the conductor's engine to Content policy (its segment tempo drives this clock) and every follower's to External.

tasks.title: Map the conductor's bar identity onto local Link beats and bridge the session clock
tasks.summary: Followers in a Link room translate (conductor bar, conductor Link micros at that downbeat) through the offset estimate into local time and snap to the nearest grid downbeat with time_at_beat, keeping a private bar-to-beat map and never re-anchoring Link; bars are about 2 s so a 100 ms offset error cannot pick the wrong bar. Where no Link peer exists but gear wants Link, `force_beat_at_time` bridges the session clock into a Link instance, the only place it is allowed.

tasks.title: Build the simulated-network transport and assert hold and rejoin under loss and jitter
tasks.summary: A test transport implementing the session transport trait that injects configurable latency, jitter, loss and reordering; the harness ships with the transport trait and the session clock so the foundation, horizon and failure-table tasks write their hold, rejoin, retract-race and claim-timeout tests on it; two- and three-station tests assert identical foundations per span and bounded late records on every PR before any soak exists.

tasks.title: Build the session panel: host or join by code, members, roles, cue requests, network
tasks.summary: Host a session or join by code or IP, see members with presence and round-trip, who conducts, offer or accept handoff, see cue requests with the sender and any collision, trust toggles and ask mode, and the wired-network recommendation with a Wi-Fi warning. A lock-mismatch reject shows the differing packs and offers 'fetch this show and rejoin', running `fetch --show` through its mirror path and reconnecting.

tasks.title: Show claims on the layer strips, the effective horizon, request senders, late records
tasks.summary: Fill the Phase 3 claim indicator (claimed by you, by Station 2, clash), add claim and release to the strips and to the mapping's `session` action, and draw the effective horizon line with 'sessions react at the next bar'. Cue requests show their sender and any collision as a local cue would; the late-record counter from the failure table is shown on the header and in the diagnostics view.

tasks.title: Serve a web status page from a headless xj-station
tasks.summary: An embedded HTTP page on the station: transport and session state, foundation timeline, members, claims, late-record and late-command counters, logs tail, and the diagnostics bundle download; read-only, LAN only.

tasks.title: Soak conductor handoffs back and forth every N segments for an hour
tasks.summary: Transfer the role between two in-process stations every N segments for an hour on the session clock; assert no gaps, no duplicate publishers, epoch continuity and identical foundations.

tasks.title: Run the eight-hour three-station soak with a headless container and a scripted performer
tasks.summary: Nightly: three headless stations, one an `xj-station` CLI in a container, eight hours on the session clock with a scripted performer sending cues and claims and injecting every row of the failure table (vanishing conductor, vanishing follower, late records, lock mismatch at hello); assert zero late records on the wired path and bounded late records on the lossy simulation, zero dropouts, valid captures on all three.

tasks.title: Play the 30-minute duet: two workstations and an MPC on Link, two handoffs, two captures
tasks.summary: In one room on a wired switch: two workstations, an MPC on Link (requires the Link license on file; otherwise the MPC follows MIDI clock from a station), a 30-minute duet with two handoffs, a human listening for drift, captures recorded on both stations and the recording published as the proof. This is the Phase 5 exit demonstration and is not automated.

tasks.title: Obtain counsel's review of live performance as output and of the venue's patent position
tasks.summary: Questions: does a paid live performance count as output audio under section 2 of the software license (the proposal assumes yes by the license's own text); what does section 3's no-patent-license clause mean for a venue running several stations that are not embedded in a commercial product; does CC BY attribution via CREDITS.md satisfy a venue's obligations. File the written position and update the licensing page; required before 2.2 ships.

tasks.title: Record the post-Phase-5 gate: did the duet work, and does the Q13 default move
tasks.summary: From the duet captures, the drift observations and the performers' feedback: decide whether Phase 7 is scheduled, whether the accept-all cue-request default stays (Q13), and what the sessions found that Phase 6 or 2.x must fix; record as a decision.

tasks.title: Write the venue setup guide: wired network, join codes, roles, failure behavior
tasks.summary: Cable, switch and mirror advice ('wired recommended' said loudly), join codes, who conducts, what the effective horizon means for cue latency in a session, every failure row and what the UI shows, and how to run a headless station.

tasks.title: Release workstation 2.2 with sessions after the legal review and the duet
tasks.summary: Tag `workstation-v2.2.0` once the duet is recorded, the legal review is filed, the protocol is published and the soaks are green.

tasks.title: Implement an undoable command stack over content edits
tasks.summary: Every edit is a command with inverse applied to the in-memory content and saved through xj-content; N-step undo and redo (#315), grouping of drag operations, and edits taking effect in the running engine at the next segment boundary through `xj_engine_reload_content`.

tasks.title: Edit one instrument name in Rust, save, and reopen the project identically in Java
tasks.summary: The Make-mode thin slice: a single rename through the command stack, saved by the canonical writer with the V2 sidecar untouched, reopened in the Java 1.9.x workstation with the parsed tree identical and the audio folder relocated by the same slug rule; undo restores the file. It exercises the R14 round-trip job with editor-produced files for the first time.

tasks.title: Implement the content CRUD service with the Java cascades, defaults and project actions
tasks.summary: Port the business rules verbatim: program type change cascades (to Main deletes tracks/patterns/events; to Macro also chords, voicings, voices; to Beat/Detail deletes bindings, binding memes, chords, voicings) with confirmation; shrinking a pattern total deletes out-of-range events after confirm; a sequence total cannot shrink below any pattern total; deleting a sequence is refused while bound or patterned; deleting a binding is refused while it has memes; new entities inherit defaults from siblings (tempo, key, type, loopBeats). Dirtiness from content hashes, not 'any view'. Project-level actions come with it: new, open, open recent, save, save as (re-homing audio), close and quit with the save prompt, and migration of the legacy single-file layout; `MakeBackend::Native` is implemented here and becomes the default with the library browser.

tasks.title: Build the library browser with create, duplicate, move, delete and navigation history
tasks.summary: Libraries, programs and instruments tables (or a tree, #319), double-click to edit, quick actions for Edit, Duplicate, Move, Delete with the Java warnings (counts of programs, instruments and bindings; 'cannot be undone' now 'undoable'), the Cmd modal equivalents, and route history. Entering Make mode opens the browser on the instrument that is playing right now (first-run step 5). It makes `MakeBackend::Native` the default, so the Make button no longer hands off to Java.

tasks.title: Build config editors validated against the C++ parser dialect and suggested meme entry
tasks.summary: Template, program and instrument config editing that validates with the exact subset the engine parses (sorted `key = value`, typed by literal shape, the ten instrument-type keys in maps checked, no comments or substitutions), optionally as a form over known keys (#323) while preserving unknown keys; a memes container with inline add, edit, delete and suggestions from memes already used in the project and xj-base (#316).

tasks.title: Build the instrument editor: fields, memes, config, audios table, import
tasks.summary: Name, type, mode (locked to valid modes per type, #339), state, volume, memes, config, open folder, the audios table with the Java columns and context actions, and import audio that creates the InstrumentAudio with inherited defaults and navigates to the audio editor.

tasks.title: Import audio in any decodable format and propose loopBeats and tempo from the file
tasks.summary: Decode with symphonia on import (WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, AAC, OGG), compute lengthSeconds from frames, content-hash the file, and for Loop-mode instruments compute fileBeats = lengthSeconds × tempo / 60 and propose loopBeats (or flag a tempo mismatch) instead of silently defaulting to 4.0, which produced 30 of the 35 bad demo loops. Store the `audio/<blake3>.toml` format sidecar.

tasks.title: Build the audio editor with waveform, transient and loop markers, zoom and all fields
tasks.summary: Name, event, volume, tones (validated by the grammar port: uppercase roots, octave required for Event mode, `X` not `x`), tempo, intensity, transientSeconds, lengthSeconds (read-only), loopBeats; a waveform with per-channel lanes, beat grid from tempo, click-to-set transient, loop-length marker, zoom; open folder and file.

tasks.title: Add pitch-shift and stretch allowance controls, inline lint fixes, and batch processing
tasks.summary: allowPitchShift with pitchShiftRange and allowStretch (enabled only when the instrument's loops pass the length rule), with the lint verdict shown inline; an instrument-scoped lint over the unsaved document with structured multi-field fixes applied as undoable edits; batch processing: import a folder as an instrument, parse tones and events from filenames by a user pattern, set fields across a selection (#329).
